items.title: We taught women to fear rape, but did we teach men not to rape?
items.description: I am here as a woman in her 40s, asking myself a question that has been on my mind since I came across the comments attributed to Daniel Nortey: “ Why are we behaving as if it is not normal to rape someone? Which man hasn’t raped a lady before?” Did he really say something we have not heard before? Something we did not grow up hearing from our peers, in our communities and sometimes even in casual conversations among adults? Many of us grew up hearing boys say things like, “A woman will say no until you force yourself on her.” Some said it jokingly. Others said it with a disturbing sense of confidence. And sometimes, those around them laughed, dismissed it as boys being boys, or simply moved on. But how many of us challenged them? How many of us stopped those conversations and explained that forcing yourself on a woman is not a sign of masculinity? How many of us made it clear that consent is not optional? Instead, we grew up in a society that spent considerable time teaching girls how to avoid being raped, but not nearly enough time teaching boys that they must never rape. We told girls to dress appropriately. We told them not to walk alone at night, not to visit certain places, not to drink too much, not to trust strangers and not to put themselves in situations where men might take advantage of them. We taught them to cover up, be careful, watch their surroundings and protect their reputations. And when a woman was sexually assaulted, one of the first questions she often faced was: “What was she wearing?” Not, “Why did he think he had the right to touch her?” Not, “Did he obtain her consent?” Not, “Why did he ignore her refusal?” But, “What was she wearing?” Somehow, we turned the conversation from the actions of the perpetrator to the appearance and behaviour of the victim. We made women feel responsible for men’s behaviour Think about the message we have repeatedly sent to girls and women over the years. If you dress a certain way, a man might attack you. If you go out at night, you are putting yourself at risk. If you are too friendly, a man might misunderstand you. If you drink, you might be blamed for what happens to you. If you are assaulted, people may examine your choices before they examine the choices of the person who assaulted you. Over time, we have created a culture in which women are expected to manage men’s sexual behaviour through their clothing, movement, speech and lifestyle. We have made women feel that their safety depends largely on how well they can avoid provoking a man. But let us ask ourselves an uncomfortable question: Why is the responsibility for preventing sexual violence placed so heavily on the potential victim rather than on the person who chooses to commit the offence? A woman can dress modestly and still be assaulted. A woman can dress in revealing clothing and still have every right to refuse sexual advances. A woman can be in a relationship, be married, or have had consensual sex with someone before and still say no. Clothing is not consent. Friendliness is not consent. Silence is not consent. Marriage is not permanent consent. And being in the same room with someone does not give that person ownership of your body. We must stop presenting women’s clothing as an explanation for men’s decision to commit sexual violence. Whatever a woman wears, the responsibility for rape lies with the person who commits it. But what were we teaching the boys? This is where the conversation becomes even more important. While we were teaching girls how to protect themselves, were we teaching boys how to respect boundaries? While we were telling girls to be careful around men, were we telling boys that a woman’s body is not theirs to claim? While we were warning daughters about the dangers of walking alone, were we having honest conversations with our sons about consent, sexual pressure, coercion and respect? Or did we assume that boys would somehow figure it out as they grew older? We cannot ignore the influence of the things boys hear among their peers, the jokes that normalise sexual aggression, the entertainment that portrays persistence as romantic, and the social expectations that suggest a man must always pursue sex, regardless of a woman’s response. Some boys are taught that a woman who says no is merely playing hard to get. Others grow up believing that persistence is proof of love, that a man must insist until a woman gives in, or that sexual conquest is a measure of manhood. These beliefs must be challenged. A boy must understand that rejection is not humiliation. A man must understand that being sexually attracted to a woman does not give him a right to her body. And every child must learn that another person’s boundaries are to be respected, not negotiated through intimidation, pressure or force. We cannot continue to excuse harmful attitudes as harmless jokes simply because they are expressed among friends. What we laugh at today can become what we tolerate tomorrow. And what we tolerate repeatedly can become a social norm that is difficult to challenge. We preached submission but sometimes neglected accountability For generations, many women have been taught to be submissive, accommodating, patient and forgiving. In relationships and marriages, women are often reminded of their responsibilities to respect and satisfy their partners. But how often do we give equal attention to the responsibility of men to respect women? How often do we teach boys that leadership does not mean control, that strength does not mean intimidation, and that masculinity does not require sexual dominance? Submission cannot mean surrendering your right to bodily autonomy. Marriage cannot mean that a woman loses the right to refuse sex. Love cannot mean that a person must endure sexual pressure to prove their commitment. And no man should be taught that his needs, desires or authority automatically take precedence over a woman’s consent. If we are serious about healthy relationships and responsible families, we must teach respect and accountability to both sexes. We cannot keep placing expectations on women while treating men’s behaviour as something women must learn to manage. Protecting the girl child is not enough Let me be clear: empowering girls and women is necessary. Teaching girls to recognise danger, defend their boundaries and report abuse matters. Providing survivors with support, protection and access to justice matters. But these measures alone cannot solve the problem. We must also raise boys who understand consent, challenge friends who make degrading comments about women, and hold perpetrators accountable for their actions. We need parents to have difficult conversations with their sons. Schools must teach respect, consent and healthy relationships in age-appropriate ways. Religious institutions, traditional leaders, the media and public figures must stop reinforcing the idea that women are responsible for preventing men’s misconduct. And when boys express harmful beliefs, we must correct them rather than excuse them. This responsibility does not belong to mothers alone. Fathers, uncles, brothers, teachers, coaches and male role models must be part of this conversation. Men must be willing to challenge other men, particularly in spaces where women are absent and harmful attitudes are expressed freely. We need boys to hear from the men they admire that a real man does not prove his masculinity by overpowering a woman. He demonstrates character by respecting her choices, including when she says no. We must stop asking the wrong questions When a woman reports sexual assault, our first response should not be to investigate her clothing, question her character or speculate about why she was in a particular place. We should listen, take the allegation seriously, support her safety and allow a fair process to establish the facts. Accountability and due process matter. Every allegation must be handled responsibly. But neither due process nor the presumption of innocence requires us to humiliate survivors or make assumptions about their clothing and behaviour. A woman’s outfit is not evidence of consent. Her decision to attend a party is not permission for sexual contact. Her decision to enter someone’s home is not an agreement to have sex. And if a woman changes her mind, her decision must be respected. We must move away from a culture that places survivors on trial while leaving the attitudes that enable sexual violence largely untouched. The conversation must change The statement attributed to Daniel Nortey should prompt us to examine more than one individual’s words. It should make us reflect on the beliefs we have heard, the jokes we have tolerated, the lessons we have taught and the harmful narratives we have allowed to survive. Rape is not normal. It is not an inevitable part of being a man. It is not a rite of passage, and it is certainly not something every man has done. We must not allow a harmful statement to define all men. Many men understand consent, respect women and actively oppose sexual violence. We need more men to speak up and help change the attitudes that enable abuse. But we must also stop pretending that harmful beliefs do not exist simply because confronting them makes us uncomfortable. For too long, we have told women to dress differently, behave differently, move differently and live differently to reduce the risk of being assaulted. Perhaps it is time to ask what we are teaching the boys who grow into the men we warn our daughters about. Perhaps we need to examine why a woman’s clothing attracts more public scrutiny than a man’s decision to disregard her refusal. Perhaps we need to acknowledge that while personal safety advice can be useful, it must never become a way of transferring responsibility for sexual violence from the perpetrator to the victim. We cannot keep teaching girls how to avoid being raped while failing to teach boys not to rape. Protect the girl child. Empower women. Support survivors. Demand accountability. But let us also raise boys who understand consent, respect boundaries and know that no woman owes them access to her body. Because until we change the narrative, we will continue treating the symptoms while neglecting the root of the problem. The question is no longer only, “How do we protect our daughters?” It must also be, “What are we doing to ensure our sons understand that women are human beings to respect, not bodies to conquer?” That is a conversation we should have started a long time ago.

items.title: US embassy staff, families ordered to leave Saudi Arabia
items.description: Washington has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. It came after a diplomatic source told AFP that “all American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy” in the Gulf kingdom. The source added that families of embassy staff had also been ordered to leave the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, all of which have been targeted by Iran during the Middle East war. US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott subsequently confirmed the order in a post on X, but said it applied to “non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only”. He linked the move to Houthi attacks on the country, including airports, saying “the safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority”. Saudi Arabia has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates. On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two. “The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others,” the ministry said in a statement. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones. In June, a four-year-old truce in Yemen’s civil war collapsed, reviving the conflict that dates back to 2014. The Saudi-led coalition has backed the internationally recognised government since 2015. – Iran explosions – The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes. Late on Wednesday, Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions in the southern Hormozgan province overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, breaking a spell of relative calm. “A few minutes ago, the sound of several explosions was heard in the Karpan area of Sirik, in Hormozgan Province,” the official IRNA news agency said. It added that “local sources have not yet disclosed the nature of these explosions”. The conflict began in late February, when the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran, killing the country’s supreme leader, along with senior military commanders. Iran has attempted to blockade the strategic waterway, demanding all ships seek its authorisation to cross. In peacetime, the Hormuz strait carried around a fifth of the world’s oil supplies. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. Vanguard News The post US embassy staff, families ordered to leave Saudi Arabia appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Incendie au marché Corona de Tambacounda : Aïssata Ba perd plus de 20 millions de FCFA
items.description: Un violent incendie survenu dans la nuit du lundi 19 octobre au marché Corona de Tambacounda a ravagé plusieurs cantines et magasins. Parmi les victimes figure Aïssata Ba, qui a perdu ses quatre boutiques et plus de 20 millions de FCFA de marchandises. Le sinistre a également coûté la vie à Pa Diallo, un homme venu lui prêter main-forte pour sauver ses biens. TAMBACOUNDA – Le regard encore marqué par la douleur, Aïssata Ba peine à mesurer l'ampleur des dégâts. En quelques heures, cette commerçante, installée depuis plusieurs années au marché Corona de Tambacounda, a vu ses quatre boutiques partir en fumée, emportant des marchandises évaluées à plus de 20 millions de FCFA. « On a fait l'inventaire le matin. En mon absence, les enfants ont bien travaillé. Ils ont enregistré un chiffre d'affaires de 20,5 millions de FCFA pour les marchandises », raconte-t-elle, encore sous le choc. Vers 21 heures, ses employés l'appellent pour l'informer que le marché est en feu. Dans l'urgence, elle leur demande de récupérer un carnet contenant les noms des clients qui lui doivent de l'argent après avoir pris des marchandises, ainsi qu'un dossier dans lequel elle avait rangé des documents, notamment des papiers de maisons. Les employés s'exécutent et déplacent les premiers bagages vers une autre cantine. Mais le répit est de courte durée : les biens ainsi mis à l'abri sont, à leur tour, gagnés par les flammes. Impuissante, la commerçante assiste à la destruction de ses marchandises et de ses effets personnels. Veuve depuis peu, elle venait tout juste de terminer sa période de veuvage de quatre mois et dix jours. À cette perte matérielle s'ajoute une tragédie humaine. Pa Diallo, venu l'aider à sortir ses marchandises, a inhalé une importante quantité de fumée. Victime d'un malaise, il est transporté à l'hôpital, où il décède. « Pa Diallo était venu m'aider à sortir les bagages, mais il a beaucoup respiré la fumée. Il a étouffé. On l'a transporté à l'hôpital. C'est là qu'il est décédé », déplore-t-elle. Malgré ce coup du sort, Aïssata Ba s'efforce de garder la foi. « C'est vrai que ce qui m'arrive est douloureux, mais cela aurait pu être encore pire. Je pouvais perdre la vie. Alhamdoulillah, je rends grâce à Dieu et je garde la foi », confie-t-elle avec résignation. Parmi les premières commerçantes à s'être installées au marché, elle avait auparavant été déguerpie de son emplacement au marché central, qu'elle dit avoir acquis pour 300 000 FCFA. Recasée au marché Corona, elle affirme avoir déboursé 400 000 FCFA pour ses trois autres cantines. Au-delà des pertes subies par les commerçants, le sinistre remet en lumière la question de l'organisation du marché et de l'accessibilité des voies de secours. Selon Aïssata Ba, les sapeurs-pompiers, arrivés sur les lieux, ont rencontré des difficultés pour accéder rapidement au site en raison de l'étroitesse des voies. La commerçante reconnaît que l'occupation anarchique de certains espaces pose problème, mais souligne la difficulté de faire respecter les règles dans un environnement où les commerçants cherchent avant tout à préserver leurs activités. « Quand tu demandes à quelqu'un de ne pas s'installer sur la voie, il te prend pour quelqu'un de méchant et t'accuse de ne pas connaître les réalités d'un marché », explique-t-elle. Pour éviter qu'un tel drame ne se reproduise, Aïssata Ba plaide pour une meilleure organisation du marché et la libération des voies de secours, afin de faciliter l'intervention des sapeurs-pompiers en cas d'urgence. Elle lance également un appel aux autorités pour accompagner les victimes de l'incendie et les aider à surmonter cette épreuve. Boubacar Agna CAMARA (correspondant)

items.title: Togo Navy alerted as Ghana works to secure return of seven missing fishermen
items.description: Authorities are working to secure the safe return of seven crew members of a missing fishing canoe, Second Chance, after their location was established within Togolese territorial waters, Western Regional Minister Joseph Nelson has disclosed. Mr Nelson said contact had been established with the crew, while Ghanaian authorities were engaging their Togolese counterparts to facilitate their return. “This afternoon, I had a briefing that some contact has been established with the crew and that their location is within Togolese waters,” he said on Accra-based Citi FM on Wednesday, October 21. “And so the Togo Navy has also been informed. Efforts are still underway to see how they can get them safely home,” he added. Mr Nelson said search and rescue operations began on Monday, October 19, after authorities received reports of the missing fishermen late on Sunday, October 18. “Late Sunday evening, we had information about these missing persons. And so Monday, the search and rescue operation commenced, and it’s been on till now,” he said. His comments follow an announcement by the Western Regional Marine Police Command that it was coordinating efforts to locate the canoe and its seven crew members after the vessel failed to return from a fishing expedition offshore Axim. The search operation involves the Ghana Navy, the Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA), the Fisheries Commission, relevant coastal police stations and fishing communities. According to the police, the canoe’s owner, Nana Kweku Atta, reported the incident at the Fishing Harbour Police Station in Sekondi on Sunday, October 18. Mr Atta told police that the canoe departed the Sekondi Fishing Harbour on Friday, October 9, for a fishing expedition offshore Axim but had failed to return as expected. Preliminary investigations indicated that repeated attempts to contact the seven crew members had been unsuccessful, raising concerns about their whereabouts. A subsequent update suggested that the canoe might have suffered engine failure at sea, potentially causing it to drift from its intended fishing grounds towards Tema and the Volta coast. The latest information that the crew had been located in Togolese waters has prompted engagement with the country’s naval authorities to facilitate their safe return to Ghana.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Plongée au cœur des préparatifs à « Kër Ayo » avec l’armée des volontaires
items.description: À l’approche des JOJ, Dakar s’active intensément et le site de « Kër Ayo », à Ouakam, ne désemplit pas. Quelque 6 000 volontaires s’y rendent pour récupérer leurs accréditations ainsi que leurs équipements. Encadrés par les team leaders, bénévoles et cuisiniers finalisent leur préparation pour relever le défi olympique. À moins de deux semaines des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse, la ville de Dakar s’est parée des couleurs de cet événement d’envergure. La capitale métamorphose son décor tandis que les préparatifs s’enchaînent à un rythme soutenu. « Kër Ayo », situé dans l’ancienne base militaire française de Ouakam, accueille du monde. Ce lieu ne rassemble pas de simples visiteurs, mais de nombreux volontaires venus effectuer les démarches pour récupérer leurs badges d’accès ainsi que leurs tenues officielles. Au total, 6 000 bénévoles ont été retenus à la suite d’un appel à candidatures publié sur le site Jambaar26, après avoir passé un entretien téléphonique préalable à leur sélection finale. Pour participer à cette aventure olympique, les critères imposaient d’avoir au moins 18 ans révolus, de maîtriser les bases du français et de l’anglais et d’assurer une disponibilité minimale de dix jours pendant toute la durée des épreuves. La répartition de ces volontaires s’effectuera sur les six sites officiels retenus pour la compétition : le Tour de l’Œuf, le stade Iba Mar Diop, la Corniche Ouest, le stade Abdoulaye Wade, la Dakar Arena et le site de Saly. Au Village olympique de la jeunesse, nommé « Kër Ayo », sis à Ouakam, l’agitation est constante. Des vagues de jeunes entrent et sortent sans interruption, sac floqué du logo des JOJ à l’épaule, pour aller chercher leur matériel. À l’intérieur du bâtiment, des panneaux guident chacun vers les espaces de distribution. 6 000 volontaires mobilisés Parmi eux, El Hadji Mamath Loum fait partie du groupe des 200 jeunes leaders sélectionnés par les Nations unies et le comité d’organisation des JOJ. Intégrés à la team événementielle, ils sont chargés de l’encadrement des 6 000 volontaires. « On gère les équipes qui se chargent de la billetterie et du spectacle. Les 200 volontaires de la team leader doivent manager les 6 000 volontaires », précise-t-il, revenant sur leurs missions. Et d’ajouter : « Chaque volontaire travaille 6 ou 7 jours sur 13. Les 200 ont subi une formation au Centre d’entraînement tactique capitaine Mbaye Diagne de Thiès. Nous avons passé 7 jours là-bas avec les militaires. » Près de la zone d’attribution des accréditations et des uniformes, des files d’attente s’organisent et de petits regroupements se forment. Sac sur l’épaule, une jeune bénévole s’apprête à quitter les lieux et nous explique sa fonction : « Je fais partie du service au spectateur, c’est nous qui les guidons. Quand ils viennent, on vérifie leurs billets et on leur indique là où ils doivent s’asseoir. » Elle apporte également des précisions sur le processus de recrutement et la suite du programme : « On a déposé en ligne et il y avait un formulaire à remplir. Après, on nous a fait passer un entretien téléphonique. Les volontaires subiront une formation dimanche prochain dans leurs sites respectifs. » L’activité à « Kër Ayo » ne se limite pas aux volontaires : les cuisiniers préposés aux repas des athlètes et des délégations viennent eux aussi récupérer leurs accréditations et uniformes. C’est le cas de Sira Badji, qui détaille son parcours : « Nous avons déposé notre candidature et, après sélection, on nous a appelés pour signer un contrat et nous avons fait une formation de 5 jours à l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar. Il y en a qui ont des contrats de 3 mois, certains de 45 jours. Pour ma part, j’ai un contrat de 3 mois. Certains sont chargés de cuisiner pour les athlètes, d’autres pour les accompagnateurs », explique-t-elle. Fatou NGOM

items.title: UCL: Why we lost 4-1 to Como – Man United’s captain Bruno Fernandes
items.description: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes said his side lacked belief as their woes continued with a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday. Man United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes declined to point the finger at his manager. “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me,” he said. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. items.title: El Mansouri : « Nous refusons que les riches s’enrichissent et les pauvres s’appauvrissent »
items.description: La cheffe du gouvernement Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a déclaré que le nouvel exécutif entendait rompre avec la trajectoire du gouvernement précédent, en raison de son « refus catégorique de laisser les riches s’enrichir davantage et les pauvres s’appauvrir davantage ». Elle a indiqué que cette nouvelle coalition soutenait la mise en place d’une économie forte et d’un environnement favorable à l’investissement, fondé sur la simplification des procédures et la réforme des mécanismes d’octroi des autorisations, selon un cahier des charges. Lors d’une séance plénière consacrée à la discussion du programme gouvernemental, qu’elle avait présenté lundi lors d’une séance conjointe des deux chambres du Parlement, El Mansouri a insisté sur « la nécessité d’encourager les entreprises, dont le rôle est central dans la création d’emplois dans notre pays et dans la dynamisation du développement, lequel garantit la stabilité et permet au Maroc de devenir un pays émergent offrant un avenir prometteur à ses enfants ». Elle a affirmé que « la volonté d’enrichir certains individus au seul motif qu’ils sont proches du pouvoir est exclue ». La cheffe du gouvernement a également défendu l’appellation de « gouvernement politique » qu’elle a choisie pour désigner la nouvelle coalition exécutive, composée de quatre partis. Selon elle, « cette qualification repose sur les références idéologiques et politiques des partis qui la composent, sur les parcours militants de plusieurs de ses membres, ainsi que sur leur engagement à écouter les citoyennes et les citoyens et à répondre à leurs attentes ». El Mansouri a répondu au président du groupe du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), qui s’était étonné de l’existence de points communs entre les composantes du nouveau gouvernement en matière de visions et de fondements théoriques. Elle a souligné que « ce qui unit les composantes de la majorité gouvernementale, c’est l’existence de références politiques et idéologiques clairement définies, ainsi que les parcours militants suivis par plusieurs de leurs membres au sein de leurs partis ». La cheffe du gouvernement a expliqué que certains ministres avaient mené des combats politiques importants, au cours desquels ils avaient affronté des luttes internes au sein de leurs partis pour s’imposer et défendre leur vision de la société. Elle a estimé que « cet esprit militant constitue l’un des éléments qui font du nouveau gouvernement un “gouvernement politique” ». Dans ce contexte, l’intervenante a rappelé que les partis politiques participant au gouvernement s’appuyaient chacun sur leurs propres références idéologiques. Elle a notamment cité le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS), le Parti de l’Istiqlal et l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), considérés comme des formations disposant de références idéologiques et politiques bien établies. La responsable gouvernementale a affirmé que la démocratie défendue par le gouvernement ne devait pas rester formelle ni se réduire à un simple slogan. Elle doit, au contraire, reposer sur le dialogue, la proximité avec les citoyennes et les citoyens, ainsi que sur l’écoute de leurs préoccupations. Elle a souligné que l’essence même de l’engagement militant et de l’action politique, tout comme la campagne électorale, reposait sur les échanges avec les citoyens et la prise en compte de leurs attentes. Évoquant les défis auxquels l’action politique est confrontée, la cheffe du gouvernement a reconnu que le taux de participation aux élections, qui s’est établi à 38 %, traduisait, selon son analyse, une crise de confiance des citoyennes et des citoyens à l’égard des institutions, notamment des institutions élues. Ce constat a constitué un élément central des consultations menées avec les composantes actuelles de la nouvelle coalition en vue de la formation du gouvernement. La responsable politique a estimé que « le principal levier pour rétablir cette confiance consiste à ancrer l’éthique dans la gestion des affaires publiques et dans la pratique politique ». Elle a affirmé que « le gouvernement ne défend pas un discours populiste, mais une conviction : celle de la nécessité d’améliorer l’économie nationale, de répondre aux attentes des citoyens et de renforcer le processus démocratique dans le pays ». En réaction à la position du Rassemblement national des indépendants au sein de la deuxième chambre du Parlement, la coordinatrice de la direction collégiale du Parti authenticité et modernité a affirmé respecter le choix du « parti de la Colombe », tout en exprimant l’espoir que ce dernier respecterait son engagement annoncé en faveur d’une opposition constructive. La cheffe du gouvernement a insisté sur le fait que l’intégrité ne constituait pas un simple slogan politique, mais une nécessité sociale, dans un contexte marqué par la montée de la colère et des protestations chez les jeunes. Ces manifestations traduisent notamment des revendications liées à la confiance dans les institutions et à la performance des acteurs politiques. S’agissant du programme gouvernemental, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri a défendu l’orientation du gouvernement consistant à proposer des mesures concrètes pour répondre aux attentes des citoyens. Elle a précisé que l’élaboration de ce programme ne s’était pas limitée à des études théoriques ni à l’attente de propositions toutes faites générées par l’intelligence artificielle, mais qu’elle s’était fondée sur l’écoute des citoyens et sur la prise en compte des réalités propres aux régions et aux provinces du pays. items.title: Over 100 students hospitalised as mysterious gas emissions hit Ogun schools again
items.description: By James Ogunnaike More than 100 students from several secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo areas of Ogun State were reportedly hospitalised on Wednesday following another incident of suspected toxic gas emissions that left students and staff struggling to breathe and fainting. The affected students were reportedly taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Schools worst affected by the latest incident included Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye, among others. A video circulating on social media showed some of the affected students fainting and being rushed to hospitals as panic spread across the affected communities. The latest incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities demanding urgent intervention to prevent further exposure. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties. “The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and had to be rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close for the day at about 11 a.m. as the situation worsened. “Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day when the situation became frightening and unbearable. The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode,” the teacher added. The teacher said parents who heard about the incident also rushed to their children’s schools to take them home amid fears over their safety. “Some parents who heard about the unfortunate incident came to pick up their children because nobody knows exactly what is happening. We also heard that the gas emissions had been occurring since April, sending hundreds of students to hospitals whenever they resurfaced,” the teacher said. Expressing concern over the repeated incidents, the teacher called on the state government to intensify efforts to establish the source of the emissions and find a lasting solution. “We are all worried about our health and the safety of our students. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas emission. The government needs to act quickly before the situation gets worse,” the teacher said. The latest occurrence is reportedly the fourth time gaseous emissions have caused panic and disrupted school activities in Ijebu land since April 2026. The first reported incident in April affected about 40 students, while more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure in May. Another 69 students were reportedly hospitalised on June 1 after another occurrence. Schools affected in previous incidents included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin, among others. The repeated incidents have raised concerns about the safety of students and staff, particularly as the emissions appear to recur in some of the same locations. Following previous incidents, Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, said the state government was working with relevant agencies and experts to determine the cause of the emissions. The governor said the Ministries of Environment and Health were collaborating with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to investigate the phenomenon. Abiodun, speaking on the matter in June, said gas analysers had been installed in affected schools following earlier incidents to determine the nature and concentration of the emissions. “Twice now, we have recorded cases of pollution in this school and some neighbouring schools. What is interesting is that the gas pollution occurred at about the same time in the affected schools—about three schools altogether—and this has happened on two separate occasions,” the governor said. He added: “Following the first occurrence, we installed gas analysers across the schools to determine the nature and concentration of the gas, which has now been confirmed to be methane.” The governor said preliminary findings pointed to possible geological factors, including fault lines, as a potential explanation for the emissions. “Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions. We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” he said. When contacted on Wednesday, the Ogun State Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was monitoring the situation. “We are on top of the situation,” he said. Also speaking on the latest incident, Kehinde Bello, a Senior Special Assistant to Governor Abiodun and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, said the emissions were linked to underground gas occurrences previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April 2026. Bello, who visited the affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo to assess the situation, said the government was working towards finding a lasting solution. He said investigations by the government had indicated that the phenomenon could be a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. However, the precise source of the emissions and the circumstances surrounding their repeated occurrence remain central concerns for residents of the affected communities. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were reportedly attending to the affected students at the general hospitals and other healthcare facilities. The latest incident has intensified calls for a conclusive investigation and effective measures to prevent further exposure, particularly in schools, where students and staff remain vulnerable to the recurring emissions. items.title: 80m Nigerian children exposed to lead poisoning – FG
items.description: The Federal Government says an estimated 80 million children in Nigeria are exposed to lead poisoning, calling for stronger measures to address the public health and environmental threat. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Salako, said this on Wednesday in Abuja at the commemoration of the 2026 International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, themed “From Detection to Prevention.” Salako said children, women of childbearing age and pregnant women were particularly vulnerable to lead exposure, which could cause serious and lasting health consequences. “It is a toxic substance capable of affecting multiple body systems, with children, women of childbearing age and pregnant women being particularly vulnerable. “Exposure can have serious and lasting consequences, while individuals may be exposed without immediate obvious symptoms. This makes prevention, early identification and timely action essential components of any national response,” he added. The minister said the government had established an Inter-Agency Working Group on Lead Poisoning Prevention and Elimination to coordinate efforts involving relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners and other stakeholders. Salako said experiences in Lagos, Ogun, Sokoto and Zamfara had highlighted different sources of exposure and the need for state-specific interventions. He cited environmental investigations in Lagos and lead exposure concerns associated with battery recycling in Ogijo, Ogun, as evidence of the need for stronger environmental and occupational controls. “We cannot treat our way out of lead poisoning; we must prevent exposure wherever possible,” the minister said. While inaugurating the Five-Year Strategic Plan on Lead Poisoning Elimination in Nigeria (2026–2030), Salako added that a costed three-year national roadmap was being developed to translate the plan’s priorities into time-bound actions. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plan is aimed at guiding stakeholders on coordinated efforts to prevent exposure, strengthen surveillance and address environmental and occupational sources. The minister identified stronger monitoring of soil, dust, water, industrial emissions and consumer products, alongside improved regulation, enforcement and laboratory capacity, as priorities. He urged states, particularly Lagos, Ogun, Zamfara and Sokoto, to develop prevention and control action plans, and called for community involvement in identifying exposure risks. He called on all stakeholders to eliminate exposure sources like lead-based paint dust, contaminated soil, unsafe work practices and unsafe water pipes. He also cautioned against lead-glazed pottery, toys, cosmetics including traditional eyeliners (tiro) and some traditional remedies. The minister listed preventive measures to include wearing protective clothing when handling items containing lead during construction, painting and recycling. He said others included daily preventive habits like handwashing, washing children’s toys, and wet-wiping floors and play areas instead of dry sweeping. “Keeping children and pregnant women away from areas where lead may be released, such as battery recycling, repair or painting areas. “Eating nutrient-dense foods high in calcium, iron and Vitamin C, which block the body from absorbing lead,” he said. Dr Sarah Ango, a UNICEF consultant, described lead poisoning as a preventable but often invisible threat to children’s health and development. She said UNICEF was committed to ending childhood lead poisoning by 2040 and was supporting government efforts to strengthen surveillance, laboratory capacity, risk communication and policy implementation. Ango emphasised that there was no safe level of lead exposure for children. “This year’s commemoration, under the theme From Detection to Prevention, provides an opportunity to move beyond identifying the problem to accelerating practical solutions that address the root causes of lead exposure,” she said. The Principal Adviser, Resolve to Save Lives, Mrs Okeoma Obasi, said the organisation had supported surveillance systems, laboratory testing capacity, evidence generation and public awareness. She described prevention as the most effective and cost-effective strategy for protecting children from lead poisoning. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, observed from Oct. 18 to Oct. 24, is aimed at raising awareness on lead exposure and promoting measures to eliminate it. items.title: SIMI summit reaches 1,000 people with health screenings, NHIS registrations in Bono
items.description: Sustainable Impact Makers International (SIMI) says its 2026 Health Equity Summit reached more than 1,000 people in the Bono Region, combining community advocacy, health education and preventive services to address barriers to healthcare access. The three-day initiative, held in Sunyani from July 23 to 25 under the theme “Health Equity in Action: From Periods to Parenthood, For All,” recorded more than 420 screening encounters across 13 service categories and completed over 500 National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) registrations. About 800 secondary school students also participated in a film screening and facilitated discussion on issues including menstrual health, consent, early marriage and school retention. In its newly released 2026 summit report, SIMI says the activities were designed to bridge the gap between people’s understanding of preventive healthcare and their ability to access services. The report cites research indicating that only 10.3% of breast cancers in Ghana are diagnosed at Stage I or II, compared with the Global Breast Cancer Initiative benchmark of at least 60%. It also references a study of male teachers aged 45 to 60 in the Sunyani Municipality, which found that although 95% recognised the benefits of prostate screening, 90% had never been screened. SIMI says the findings highlight the need to address barriers that prevent people from translating health awareness into action. The report further notes that adolescent pregnancy in the former Brong-Ahafo Region, which included the present-day Bono Region, remained above the national average across three decades of surveys. It also identifies the limited representation of traditional and religious authorities in formal health governance as a concern, given their influence on community attitudes and health-seeking behaviour. SIMI organised the summit around three priorities: mobilising communities, empowering people through education and dialogue, and enabling access to preventive health services. The programme opened with a 5-kilometre community advocacy walk intended to raise awareness of health equity and encourage collective responsibility for community wellbeing. A subsequent policy dialogue brought together health professionals, policymakers, educators, traditional authorities and faith leaders to discuss community health priorities and possible responses. At Sunyani Senior High School, a screening of NAWI , followed by a facilitated discussion, provided students with an opportunity to engage with issues including menstrual health, consent, early marriage and school retention. The summit’s service component was delivered in partnership with the Ghana Health Service, Bono Regional Hospital and other clinical teams. It offered health screenings, health promotion activities and NHIS registration. According to SIMI, bringing the services closer to residents provided practical opportunities for participants to act on health information and access preventive care. SIMI calls for stronger referral pathways Beyond the immediate activities, the report emphasises the need for effective referral systems to ensure that people who undergo screening can access further assessment and appropriate treatment when necessary. It also introduced the Sunyani Pledge: 90-Day Health Equity Challenge, inviting participants to commit to achievable actions within their communities and institutions. SIMI says the initiative provides a foundation for continued collaboration among communities, healthcare providers, policymakers and traditional and religious leaders. The full report outlines the summit’s delivery figures, priorities identified by community members, limitations and recommendations for advancing health equity in the Bono Region and beyond. https://canva.link/simi-health-equity-summit-2026-full-report

items.title: Archevêché de Dakar: le directeur général du « Soleil » reçu par Mgr André Guèye
items.description: Le directeur général du Soleil, Lamine Niang, à la tête d’une forte délégation, a été reçu hier par Mgr André Guèye, archevêque de Dakar. Au cours de cette rencontre, ils ont passé en revue différents points relatifs à la couverture médiatique des événements religieux catholiques, ainsi que la nécessité de revisiter les archives de l’Église avec le concours du quotidien national. C’est dans une ambiance détendue et joviale que l’archevêque de Dakar, Mgr André Guèye, a reçu la délégation du « Soleil », conduite par son directeur général, Lamine Niang. Au cours de cette rencontre, ce dernier est largement revenu sur les missions et les orientations du journal. « Nous sommes là aujourd’hui pour recueillir vos conseils et vos avis afin d’améliorer notre mission de service public. Le chef de l’État tient beaucoup à l'équité dans le service public. Nous sommes donc là pour vous écouter et recueillir vos orientations afin de mieux servir la population », a souligné d’emblée M. Niang. Abordant la couverture médiatique des événements religieux catholiques, il a fait part à l’archevêque de Dakar des innovations apportées dans le traitement de manifestations telles que le pèlerinage aux lieux saints de la chrétienté et le pèlerinage marial de Popenguine, entre autres. « En plus des envoyés spéciaux pour la couverture du pèlerinage de Popenguine, nous avons innové en produisant un magazine exclusivement dédié à cet événement, comme nous le faisons pour les autres foyers religieux. Chaque année, la direction générale du Soleil octroie également un billet pour le pèlerinage aux lieux saints de la Chrétienté », a-t-il précisé. Poursuivant son propos, il a assuré qu’il compte poursuivre ces innovations en exploitant les archives du « Soleil » portant sur l’Église catholique sénégalaise. « Nous avons récemment lancé une maison d’édition et il serait très intéressant de plonger dans l’histoire de l’Église à travers les archives du « Soleil ». Nous avons des photos et des textes sur le parcours de personnalités religieuses. Nous choisirons un moment opportun pour organiser une exposition sur ces archives, car nous détenons de véritables trésors, notamment sur la visite du Pape Jean-Paul II », a précisé Lamine Niang. Après l’exposé de M. Niang, Mgr André Guèye a salué le travail remarquable du journal au quotidien, et surtout lors des événements religieux de la communauté catholique du Sénégal. Mgr André Guèye reçoit la délégation du Soleil Par ailleurs, l’archevêque a apprécié la démarche inclusive du « Soleil » sur le plan du traitement de l’information. Selon lui, « Le Soleil » est un hub d’excellence avec des journalistes talentueux qui font un travail remarquable. « Je suis un abonné du Soleil, je le reçois tous les jours. C'est pour dire que j'apprécie le travail. On a eu de grands noms au Soleil et vous en faites partie », a-t-il affirmé en s’adressant au directeur général. « Je prie pour que votre passage soit indélébile dans l'histoire du Soleil », a-t-il ajouté. Il n’a pas manqué de saluer les différentes thématiques abordées dans le journal, notamment les « Feuilles d’hivernage ». En fidèle lecteur, il a plaidé pour le retour de rubriques comme la « Pensée du jour » ou la « Citation du jour ». « C’est très important de revisiter les archives, avec des photos et des documentations qui ont marqué l'histoire du Sénégal. Il faut exposer cette richesse ; peut-être qu'il y a des photos concernant l'Église dont nous ne soupçonnons même pas l’existence », a-t-il argumenté. Il estime qu’exposer ces œuvres dans un musée permettrait aux gens de venir visiter et de se ressourcer, au lieu de rester collés aux écrans. Revenant sur le contenu du journal, Mgr Guèye a conseillé de faire en sorte que « Le Soleil » brille pour tout le monde. « Le Soleil doit être à l'image du pays. Chacun doit s'y retrouver sans distinction ni exclusion », a-t-il martelé. Profitant de l’occasion, il a exhorté les travailleurs à plus d'engagement, d’efficacité et de loyauté, tout en priant pour la prospérité du journal « afin que les rayons du Soleil brillent encore». items.title: Kankan : huit personnes condamnées pour détention, vente et consommation de chicha
items.description: Le tribunal de première instance de Kankan a rendu son verdict, ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026, dans une affaire liée à l’interdiction de la chicha en Guinée. Huit personnes ont été condamnées à des peines d’emprisonnement et à des amendes pour détention, consommation ou vente d’accessoires de ce produit. La lutte contre la chicha se poursuit en Guinée. À Kankan, huit individus interpellés lors d’une opération de police ont été traduits devant la justice, en application des dispositions légales relatives à l’interdiction du tabac et de ses dérivés. L’audience s’est tenue ce mercredi au tribunal de première instance de Kankan. Les prévenus ont été répartis en trois groupes, selon les faits qui leur étaient reprochés. Selon le procureur de la République près le tribunal, Ibrahima I. Camara, qui a communiqué les détails du jugement à la presse, les trois premiers prévenus, Namadja Diallo, Amadou Condé et Mohamed Camara, ont été reconnus coupables de détention et de consommation de chicha. Ils ont chacun écopé de 10 jours d’emprisonnement et d’une amende de 500 000 francs guinéens. Le tribunal a également ordonné la destruction par incinération des appareils de chicha et des charbons saisis. Les deux prévenus du deuxième groupe, Younoussa Baldé et Tidiane Traoré, ont été condamnés aux mêmes peines pour des faits similaires de détention et de consommation de chicha, soit 10 jours d’emprisonnement et 500 000 francs guinéens d’amende chacun. Quant au troisième groupe, composé de Mohamed Kourouma, Alhassane Keïta et Abdramane Kaba, il a été poursuivi pour détention et vente d’accessoires de chicha. Les trois hommes ont été condamnés à deux mois d’emprisonnement avec sursis et à une amende d’un million de francs guinéens chacun. « On avait fait une réquisition dans le cadre de l’interdiction de la chicha en République de Guinée. En application de la loi 039 du 15 novembre 2012, concernant l’interdiction du tabac en République de Guinée, ils ont été condamnés », a expliqué le procureur Ibrahima I. Camara. À travers ces condamnations, les autorités judiciaires de Kankan entendent contribuer à l’application de la réglementation en vigueur sur le tabac et ses dérivés. Cette affaire illustre la volonté des autorités de faire respecter l’interdiction de la chicha, présentée comme un enjeu de santé publique.

items.title: France : l’incohérence de l’extrême droite face aux « Français de papier »
items.description: Chaque événement en France, d'ampleur ou anodin, donne à constater l'incohérence chronique de la grande famille de l’extrême-droite qui englobe désormais un large faisceau de formations et de personnages politiques, allant du parti fondé par Jean-Marie Le Pen jusqu'à beaucoup de ceux qui se réclament encore de la « droite républicaine » et des personnages du centre de l’échiquier politique. Toutes ces voix dénoncent à l’unisson les actes de saccage et de violence qui ont émaillé les manifestations contre la vie chère du samedi 17 octobre et s’offusquent que des jeunes Français fassent preuve d'« incivisme » et s'attaquent aux édifices publics de leur propre pays. « Français de papier » : des Juifs aux musulmans Des jeunes que ces mêmes voix n’ont de cesse de traiter, depuis quelques années, de « Français de papier ». La responsabilité de ce qui arrive incombe aussi, et surtout, à un discours qui a trop longtemps stigmatisé, marginalisé et essentialisé une frange entière de la population française. L'expression « Français de papier » n'est ni d’Éric Zemmour ni de Bruno Retailleau ni de tous ceux qui, matin, midi et soir, tapent sur l’immigré, le musulman, l’Africain, le Maghrébin ou l’Algérien. Elle est née à une autre époque, lointaine, celle de la France antisémite de l’entre-deux-guerres. L'expression d'origine était « Français de papier timbré ». Elle désignait le Juif. Aujourd'hui, le descendant d’immigrés , précisément ceux qui ont des origines musulmanes ou africaines. De l’antisémitisme à l’islamophobie, le racisme n’a fait que changer de nom. Et de cible évidemment. « Français de papier » contre « Français de cœur » Le « Français de papier » est opposé au « Français de cœur ». La trouvaille est de Valérie Pécresse, de la droite dite « républicaine ». Comme quoi, la stigmatisation des immigrés et de leurs descendants n'est plus l'apanage de l’extrême-droite en France. Elle est partagée par un large pan de la classe politique. Elle ne cible pas que les « casseurs » ou les « dealers » des quartiers populaires, mais aussi ceux qui ont porté haut les couleurs de la France, comme le footballeur Karim Benzema. Quand on est d'origine algérienne, musulmane, africaine ou maghrébine, on est « Français de papiers » et on le reste, quoi qu'on fasse. En plus de vivre dans des quartiers défavorisés, d’être discriminés à l’emploi et dans d'autres domaines, les jeunes des banlieues entendent quotidiennement un discours qui leur rappelle qu’ils ne sont pas tout à fait Français, qu’ils sont différents du reste de la population, celle que la terminologie du courant xénophobe classe dans la case des « Français de souche ». Les faits divers sont traités par une grande partie des médias suivant qu'ils sont commis ou non par un Français issu de l’immigration. Le premier élément scruté dans un crime, pour déterminer s’il doit occuper les Unes et les plateaux ou être relégué à quelques lignes dans la case des faits divers, c’est le prénom du présumé auteur. Il en est ainsi depuis plusieurs années dans une galaxie entière de médias, dont la mission première est de porter la montée de l’extrême-droite en promouvant son discours xénophobe. La violence naît aussi de l’exclusion et du rejet Pendant les dernières manifestations des lycéens, la violence policière s’est abattue sur les « jeunes racisés des banlieues » plus que sur les autres. Le constat et l’expression sont du syndicat français des magistrats. Cette discrimination entre les citoyens français dans le discours et sur le terrain, il est arrivé au courant extrémiste de proposer de l’institutionnaliser. En juillet 2024, en pleine bataille électorale des législatives, Jordan Bardella et Marine Le Pen ont proposé d'exclure les binationaux de certaines fonctions dans les secteurs stratégiques. Ce sont ces mêmes personnages qui, aujourd'hui, sont aux avant-lignes de l’indignation du soi-disant peu d’intégration, de civisme et de patriotisme de ceux qu'ils ont décrétés moins Français que les autres ou pas du tout Français. Quand bien même il y aurait une grande proportion de jeunes issus de l’immigration parmi les émeutiers – ce qui reste à démontrer par des chiffres implacables –, leur comportement, sans être justifié, s'explique : la violence naît aussi de l’exclusion et du rejet. La violence verbale qu’une partie de l’élite française exerce, en toute liberté, à longueur de journée sur les plateaux télé réservés à la stigmatisation de l’autre, produit de la violence physique. L’article France : l’incohérence de l’extrême droite face aux « Français de papier » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Asutifi North sound system operators demand justice for allegedly assaulted colleague
items.description: Sound system operators in the Asutifi North District of the Ahafo Region are demanding the arrest and investigation of two prison officers and three inmates allegedly involved in an attack that left their colleague, Opoku Afriyie, severely injured. The group is calling on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Minister for the Interior and national security authorities to intervene, saying more than a month after the incident, the suspects have not been arrested. Afriyie, a sound system operator, commercial motorbike rider and farmer, was allegedly attacked with machetes by the two officers and three inmates from the Kenyasi Settlement Camp Prison over allegations of yam theft. The operators say the absence of arrests and a public update from the Ahafo Regional Police Command has heightened frustration among residents and could deepen tensions between the community and law enforcement. Speaking to JoyNews in Kenyasi on Tuesday, Clement Austin, a social event moderator with Emmanuel Sounds, said the suspects should be held accountable under the law. He said the Constitution guarantees equality before the law and the protection of human rights and dignity, adding that the allegations against Afriyie did not justify the reported attack. Mr Austin called on the police to arrest the suspects, insisting that no one should be treated as guilty without evidence and due process. Kwame Bandasco of Great Vim Ventures warned that further delays could trigger legal action and sustained civil pressure on the Ghana Prisons Service in the district. He said the group had been demanding arrests and justice since the incident and insisted that the two prison officers should be investigated immediately. DJ Slim of Pomaa Sounds also questioned why no arrests had been made, arguing that a civilian accused of attacking prison officers and inmates would likely have faced swift police action. The operators further alleged that management of the Kenyasi Settlement Camp Prison had approached traditional leaders, religious figures and politicians in the region to mediate an out-of-court settlement on behalf of the suspects. They have cautioned those leaders against intervening to settle the matter outside the formal justice system, citing what they describe as a history of unresolved abuses involving security personnel in the district. The group wants the police to investigate the incident and allow the legal process to proceed, saying accountability is necessary to restore confidence and prevent further tensions. The allegations against the prison officers and inmates have not been established in court. The group’s account of the incident and the alleged attempts at mediation could not be independently verified from the information available. Afriyie, who is recovering slowly at home, says the injuries have left him unable to work and provide for his family. In an interview with JoyNews, he said he now relies on the support of neighbours and loved ones to care for his wife, children and 80-year-old mother. The father and farmer, who owns three farms, said the attack had disrupted his livelihood and left his family struggling to meet their daily needs. The operators say they will continue pressing the authorities to act until the case is investigated and justice is pursued through the formal legal system.

items.title: SEAT réaffirme sa présence au Maroc et son engagement durable auprès de ses clients
items.description: Dans un contexte marqué par différentes informations concernant l’avenir de SEAT, la marque souhaite réaffirmer sa présence sur le marché marocain et rassurer ses clients quant à la continuité de ses activités, de son réseau et de l’accompagnement qui leur est proposé. SEAT est aujourd’hui une marque active et pleinement présente au Maroc. La marque continue d’accompagner ses clients à travers son réseau et poursuit la commercialisation de véhicules reconnus pour leur qualité, leur technologie et leur rapport qualité-prix, avec une feuille de route produit claire pour les années à venir. Comme l’ensemble de l’industrie automobile, SEAT évolue dans un environnement en profonde transformation, marqué notamment par l’électrification, l’évolution de la réglementation et les nouvelles attentes des clients. Dans ce contexte, plusieurs scénarios concernant l’avenir à long terme de la marque restent à l’étude au-delà de 2030. Ces réflexions ne remettent toutefois pas en cause les activités actuelles de SEAT ni les engagements pris auprès de ses clients. SEAT bénéficie de son appartenance à SEAT S.A. et au Groupe Volkswagen, groupe automobile de référence à l’échelle internationale. Cet ancrage permet à la marque de s’appuyer sur les technologies, le savoir-faire et l’expertise du Groupe. Au Maroc, SEAT est importée par la Centrale Automobile Chérifienne, leader de la distribution automobile. Grâce à son réseau de partenaires solide et sa stratégie orientée client, la CAC continue de s’engager sur la qualité de l’expérience client auprès des acquéreurs de la marque SEAT au Maroc. Un accompagnement client pleinement assuré Pour les propriétaires actuels comme pour les clients qui envisagent l’acquisition d’une SEAT, les engagements de la marque restent inchangés. Les garanties en cours restent valables conformément aux conditions contractuelles applicables. Les services Après-Vente, l’entretien des véhicules ainsi que l’approvisionnement en pièces de rechange continuent également d’être assurés à travers le réseau agréé. L’activité des concessions et des Partenaires Service SEAT se poursuit normalement. Aucun changement n’affecte les activités de Vente ou d’Après-Vente de la marque. SEAT poursuit par ailleurs l’évolution de son offre. Les nouvelles versions de l’Ibiza et de l’Arona illustrent notamment la continuité de cette dynamique dans les années à venir. Les Best seller de la marque que sont l’ATECA et la LEON en motorisation Diesel sont également disponibles sur le marché marocain pour satisfaire la demande de la clientèle sur ces segments. À travers cette prise de parole, SEAT souhaite réaffirmer un message essentiel : la marque est aujourd’hui présente au Maroc et le sera demain, ses activités se poursuivent et ses clients continuent de bénéficier de l’accompagnement de son réseau et de ses services, avec le soutien de SEAT S.A. et du Groupe Volkswagen. The post SEAT réaffirme sa présence au Maroc et son engagement durable auprès de ses clients appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — Health Minister
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Presidential Task Force on Ebola said on Wednesday that the Nigerian government is collaborating with its Ugandan counterpart to contain any outbreak of Ebola. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this while fielding questions from journalists at the end of a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila. Asked to react to the statement credited to Ugandan authorities that the country does not have any case of Ebola, contrary to reports that a Nigerian woman contracted the virus in Uganda, the Minister said: “All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation, Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures in place to ensure that it does not enter our population.” He said the Federal Government has competent authorities to deal with the development, adding: “We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions. “Nigerians should be reassured. We must be vigilant, but not panic. People should respect public health information from trusted sources and not spread misinformation and false rumours. “We would be truthful to Nigerians with the information that we receive on a daily basis. I will be receiving a report. The NCDC has an incident management system.” The Minister said the NCDC is working hard and that the task force is also active. “So, we have things in place that give us confidence that Nigeria can weather this public health crisis, which has taken five months without happening, and we have seen other countries also deal with it. “So, let us not fall into the trap of hysteria or panic. It is one case. It is an imported case, and we are containing it. And we will continue to take measures. If the situation changes, we will come out and inform Nigerians.” He said that at the last Security Council meeting, there was a push, with the President, to review response plans. “The truth of the matter is that we have a very good response coordination mechanism involving the Office of the NSA, public health measures and the task force, and that has served us well. “In fact, we are a large country, and I travel a lot. We have one case, and even that one case came from outside our country. We have been able to detect it, report it and take efforts to contain it. We should not fall into the trap of panic or hysteria, which is counterproductive. “But we have to be vigilant, and that is what we are doing. In the last 24 hours, we have been on top of it. I am going back to a meeting. We will have another meeting tomorrow (today), so we are on top of it because health security is very important, and we will continue to do that. “We will be focused. There is a lot of noise from even those who have no idea. Today, just a couple of hours ago, I spoke to the person who discovered the virus 50 years ago. “It is a 50-year-old virus, and it has had multiple outbreaks in the past. There have been almost 10 or 11 different outbreaks, and they were able to contain them. “Kenya has been able to contain it. Uganda was able to contain it. France was also able to contain it. But in Nigeria, because people do not think beyond Nigeria, whenever they hear of something new, everybody panics. We cannot be complacent. “Absolutely, we have to focus. We have to execute. It requires discipline. It is not talk; it is actually doing what is needed. We have the resources, we have the backing of our President, and we have the mechanisms across institutions. “So, we will continue. Now, it is also left for people to behave responsibly, because if somebody knows something and you say, ‘Oh, isolate yourself,’ and then you hide behind the door and go out to the market, that is not in the government’s hands.” The post Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — Health Minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed by Russia as Trump envoy meets Putin
items.description: Russia released a 74-year-old American citizen who was jailed for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine, as President Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg for talks. Stephen Hubbard had been taken to the city’s Pulkovo Airport, Putin said during the meeting early on Wednesday. President Donald Trump later said the former teacher was “on his way back home” and “there was no ‘swap’ necessary”. Following the release, Witkoff called Putin a humanitarian. Hubbard, who was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony in 2024, was accused of serving in a defence unit in eastern Ukraine when he was captured in 2022, shortly after Russia’s full-scale invasion. CBS News, the BBC’s US media partner, reported that Hubbard had been in poor health and was expected to be flown to Texas for treatment. Witkoff gave praise to Putin for releasing Hubbard, saying: “You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian – you are a humanitarian also sir, and I salute that. I commend you.” His comments sparked a backlash from lawmakers in the Republican party, with Representative Don Bacon posting on social media that it was “another embarrassment”. Senator John Cornyn said Putin “is a stone cold killer”. In response to a question from the BBC about the backlash, Vice President JD Vance said Witkoff’s “job is to go over there and get a job done”. “I care much less about what Steve said than about the fact that he is bringing an American hostage home to his family,” he said during a press conference in Ohio on Wednesday. Hubbard was later seen thanking Witkoff as they met separately. Putin’s financial adviser Kirill Dmitriev was also present. Writing on social media after Russian state media reported the release, Trump said it had followed a request he “made directly” to Putin last week. In the past, detained Americans have primarily been released from Russia through prisoner swaps. Trump also appeared to defend his recent decision to suspend sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to come into force, writing that “if sanctions would have been placed”, negotiations for Hubbard’s release “would have come to a complete and total halt”. The US state department had previously classified Hubbard, from Michigan, as “wrongfully detained” and Trump on Tuesday had suggested that his release may be imminent. “Watch what happens,” Trump told reporters, “we have been focused ⁠on ​Hubbard”. The state department said in a statement that the release was “a welcome step that we hope leads to the release of all Americans unjustly held in Russia”. It also said that “there are currently no Americans determined to be wrongfully detained in Russia”. Russian prosecutors had accused Hubbard of joining a Ukrainian military unit and receiving training and weapons. But his sister, Patricia Fox Hubbard, previously told Reuters that this was unlikely because of his older age and his disinterest in the military. Hubbard’s son, Joseph Coleman, who is an Orthodox priest, said in a statement that he had prayed for many years for his father’s release. “As I await the blessing of embracing him again, I receive his freedom not as a political victory, but as a gift of mercy,” Coleman said. A lawyer for Hubbard, Martin De Luca, posted on social media on Wednesday: “The road to peace is difficult, but its human dividends need not wait for a final agreement.” A spokesman for Putin, Dmitry Peskov, told Russian media that American officials had been seeking Hubbard’s for some time, and Putin decided to do it for humanitarian reasons. Witkoffalsothanked Putin for the deal struck with Washington earlier this month to import Russian diesel , saying Trump was “deeply grateful” for it. Ahead of the US midterm elections in November, where affordability is top issue for many voters, Trump has sought to bring down fuel costs. The first shipment under the agreement will leave Russia “in two to three days”, Putin said during the meeting, as quoted by state news agency TASS. The diesel dealinfuriated Zelenskyand triggered a tumultuous few weeks of deteriorating relations during which Trump suspended a number of sanctions and said it was time for Ukraine to elect a new leader. Kyiv meanwhile accused Washington of halting intelligence sharing on deadly Russian strikes, and claimed a sudden restriction to the Starshield internet service in its war effort had been deliberate. Zelensky said on Tuesday that intelligence sharing had resumed. As talks were under way in St Petersburg, Zelensky posted on social media that “much depends on whether the American side can hear something new from Russia today – about peace, and not about continuing the war”.

items.title: The AI-Hacking Apocalypse Began Last Night
items.description: The internet could be on the verge of a total meltdown. Yesterday, someone posted to a public forum that two major security flaws had been found in a programming language that undergirds the web. The language, called PHP, is used by as much as 70 percent of websites. In order to protect themselves from hackers, a number of government, hospital, and school websites across Europe went dark this morning. The organization that maintains PHP quickly confirmed it was preparing to announce two major vulnerabilities alongside patches for them. Both weaknesses, officially disclosed today, appear to have existed in PHP for more than a decade but were only just discovered with the use of AI tools. Hackers have already been detected trying to exploit them, likely with the help of AI, and implementing the fixes to address the vulnerabilities could take companies days or weeks. In the meantime, tens of millions of servers, databases, and devices are exposed. “PHP is one of the fundamental pieces of technology that supports the internet,” Sam Rubin, a senior vice president at the cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, told me. As of now, the websites of the Finnish health agency, the Port of Rotterdam, the Paris police force, 4Chan, and an unknown number of others are all down while they address the PHP vulnerabilities. [ Read: How long until AI hacks everything? ] News of these weaknesses in PHP is the capstone in a weeks-long slew of devastating, AI-powered cybersecurity events. In recent weeks, criminals and state-backed attackers have used AI to hack into more than 100 companies, including John Deere and SharkNinja; to automate hacks on some 400 financial institutions in Latin America; and to steal hundreds of thousands of credit-card records from two companies. Since this summer, attackers have hit governments, data centers, and hospitals in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, Bangladesh, and Indonesia. Also today, the developers of Node—a platform used by nearly half of software developers—disclosed multiple high-severity vulnerabilities. And that’s the abridged list. For the better part of a year, cybersecurity experts have been warning , with mounting alarm , about an impending cyber-apocalypse . It may have begun. For decades, the internet has been riddled with holes and bugs. Code is finicky, and the standard IT approach has been to fix problems when they arise. For decades, the balance held: Skilled hackers are few, and finding and exploiting vulnerabilities takes time. Recent advances in AI have totally upended that equilibrium. Top models have become very good at finding holes and writing malware, and can work much faster than even a team of humans. This is true of both open-source AI systems from China, which can be downloaded and used without restrictions, and the even more capable models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which are continually being jailbroken. The rate of software vulnerabilities identified per month has doubled over the past year. Meanwhile, the time that hackers need to begin exploiting those vulnerabilities—figuring out how to break in and out without being caught—has fallen, by some estimates, from weeks to hours. An actual intrusion, if automated with AI, can take as little as 39 seconds . Historical approaches to detecting and fixing vulnerabilities, or monitoring for suspicious internal activity, are insufficient. AI has created new vulnerabilities, but it also promises to fix them: The vulnerabilities in PHP were discovered independently by a Google-owned cybersecurity company and another effort led by OpenAI. Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic, along with other tech firms, are all working with government agencies around the world to shore up their defenses. But, as numerous cybersecurity experts have told me, there is an asymmetry between attackers and defenders that AI is going to exacerbate: Hackers will use new technology with abandon, while companies are methodical and risk-averse—a hospital or electrical grid can’t risk that an AI security tool unintentionally takes a patient off life support or causes a brownout. And attackers need to find only one hole to succeed, whereas defenders need only one oversight to fail. For a year, criminals and state-backed groups have been experimenting with how to use models to accelerate and automate their attacks. It was only a year ago that Anthropic announced , with great consternation, what it declared to be the first instance of AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage. That still involved a lot of human oversight and required jailbroken Claude agents to work for many hours. Now that the agents are faster and more capable, hackers have gotten more adept at deploying them, and the automation is more extensive. Recent, widespread attacks on South Korean and Japanese websites were reportedly executed by a single Chinese cybercriminal who used AI to target more than 1,000 websites. “This certainly will not be the last large-scale vulnerability identified, because of what’s possible with AI,” Rubin said. The past 24 hours represent a tipping point. Bulking up IT departments, implementing passkeys, and using two-factor authentication remain important. But the most urgent and practical advice being given now is to retreat: Prepare to simply go offline. The NSA advised companies that cannot immediately fix the PHP vulnerability to take down affected digital services. Hospitals, water utilities, and other crucial services are all preparing for hacks by relearning to operate analog. Store your data in fewer places. We’re running out of time to prepare for the AI-hacking deluge. The dam may have already broken.
