items.title: Mustapha Gbande, Joseph Yammin file nominations to retain NDC positions
items.description: Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Mustapha Gbande, and National Organiser Joseph Yammin have filed their nominations to contest for re-election in the party’s upcoming National Executive Elections scheduled for December 19. The two party executives are seeking to retain their respective positions on the NDC’s National Executive Board as the party prepares for the internal elections. Speaking at the maiden edition of the Campaign Trail, an initiative by the NDC’s Elections Directorate, the two outlined their reasons for seeking another term in office. Mustapha Gbande used the platform to tout what he described as the achievements of President John Mahama’s administration since returning to power in 2025, while criticising the previous Akufo-Addo government. He said the NDC government had made progress across various sectors, adding that he was proud to have contributed to the party’s return to power. The joint press briefing provided both executives an opportunity to make their case for re-election as they seek to maintain their positions within the party’s national leadership. The December 19 elections are expected to determine the composition of the NDC’s National Executive Board as the party continues its internal reorganisation.

items.title: Faire monde ensemble (Par Lamine NIANG)
items.description: Dans son entretien au « Soleil » que nous publions aujourd’hui, le chef de l’État raconte ce souvenir avec une émotion qui dépasse l’anecdote personnelle. Il ne s’agit pas seulement de célébrer le chemin parcouru par un enfant devenu président. Il s’agit de comprendre ce qu’un événement sportif peut déposer dans l’imagination d’un jeune être. Une image, une admiration, un rêve. Et, longtemps après, la possibilité de se croire capable d’aller plus loin que l’horizon familier. Dakar 2026 doit être jugé à cette aune. Bien sûr, il faudra des compétitions réussies, des installations fonctionnelles, des transports fluides, des rues propres et une organisation à la hauteur de l’événement. Le monde ne manque pas de grands discours sur l’hospitalité. Il sait aussi mesurer le sérieux d’un pays au temps perdu dans les embouteillages, à la qualité de l’accueil dans les stades et au soin apporté aux détails. La Teranga ne saurait être un slogan imprimé sur une affiche. Elle doit se reconnaître dans les gestes. Mais les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse ne se réduisent pas à une démonstration de savoir-faire. Ils offrent au Sénégal une occasion plus rare. Celle de faire entrer ses enfants dans le monde par le contact direct avec d’autres jeunesses. D’autres langues. D’autres ambitions. Une fille de Kolda pourra voir une championne de son âge manier le fleuret. Un garçon de Pikine découvrira peut-être que l’aviron, l’escrime ou l’athlétisme ne sont pas des disciplines réservées à des contrées lointaines. Il suffit parfois d’une heure dans une tribune pour déplacer les limites que l’on s’était assignées. L’enjeu est considérable dans un pays très jeune comme le nôtre. On parle trop souvent de la jeunesse comme d’une difficulté à résoudre. D’une impatience à contenir. Dakar 2026 devrait nous aider à changer de regard. La jeunesse n’est pas seulement l’avenir du pays. Elle en est déjà le présent, avec ses talents, ses frustrations, son énergie et son besoin de perspectives. Lui offrir une scène ne dispense pas de lui ouvrir des portes. Encore faut-il que les rêves suscités par les Jeux trouvent, après la cérémonie de clôture, des chemins pour se réaliser. Le Président Faye insiste, à juste titre, sur la continuité de l’État. Les Jeux ont été attribués au Sénégal en 2018. Ils ont ensuite été reportés en raison de la pandémie. Entre-temps, les majorités ont changé, mais l’engagement demeure. Cette fidélité à la parole publique mérite d’être saluée. Un pays ne se construit pas en effaçant ce que ses prédécesseurs ont entrepris. Il se bâtit aussi en sachant reprendre un projet, le mener à son terme et en assumer la responsabilité collective. Lire aussi: Bassirou Diomaye Faye sur les joj : « Je veux qu’on dise que c’est ici que cela a commencé » La République n’appartient pas à ceux qui l’administrent momentanément. Elle survit à leurs ambitions et à leurs désaccords. Dans une période d’ajustement économique, la question du coût des Jeux reste néanmoins légitime. Chaque franc public doit être employé avec discernement, et la fête ne saurait faire oublier les urgences sociales. La meilleure réponse ne viendra pas des seules déclarations d’intention. Elle se lira dans l’usage durable des équipements, tout comme dans les compétences acquises. Elle s’appréciera dans les entreprises mobilisées, les emplois créés et les possibilités offertes aux jeunes. Une piscine olympique, un stade ou une salle omnisports n’ont de véritable valeur que s’ils continuent de servir la population longtemps après le départ des délégations. Le bilan des Jeux se mesurera autant à ce qui restera qu’à ce qui aura brillé. Pour l’Afrique, l’événement revêt une dimension supplémentaire. Elle accueille pour la première fois les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse. Pourtant, il aura fallu attendre plus d’un siècle après la naissance de l’Olympisme moderne pour que la flamme prenne rendez-vous sur cette terre. Elle a pourtant donné au sport mondial tant de champions et de moments mémorables. Cette attente dit quelque chose des déséquilibres persistants de la scène internationale. Le vieux continent a longtemps été convié à admirer, à participer, à applaudir. Le voici appelé à organiser, à décider et à recevoir. Il ne s’agit pas de transformer Dakar en procès permanent de l’ordre mondial. Il s’agit de comprendre qu’un rendez-vous sportif peut aussi porter une ambition politique, au sens le plus noble du terme. Quand un continent démontre sa capacité à accueillir une compétition de cette ampleur, il ne gagne pas seulement en visibilité. Il affirme son droit à prendre sa place. La revendication d’une représentation plus juste de l’Afrique dans les institutions internationales obéit à la même logique. On ne peut prétendre construire un monde commun en maintenant durablement à l’écart ceux qui en constituent une part majeure. Le sport, lui, propose une leçon simple, presque enfantine, mais dont les adultes feraient bien de se souvenir. On peut affronter un adversaire sans le mépriser. Défendre son drapeau sans nier celui du voisin. Chercher la victoire tout en acceptant des règles communes. Lire aussi: JOJ 2026 : Bassirou Diomaye Faye veut faire de Dakar un rendez-vous pour l’Afrique Le vaincu mérite autant de considération que le vainqueur, surtout au moment où il se relève. Dans une époque traversée par les conflits, les replis identitaires et les crispations nationales, cette grammaire du respect n’est pas dérisoire. Elle rappelle que la compétition n’exclut pas la fraternité et que la différence n’interdit pas la rencontre. Faire monde ensemble, c’est précisément cela. Ce n’est pas gommer les identités, uniformiser les cultures ou prétendre que les inégalités disparaissent le temps d’une cérémonie. C’est reconnaître que nous partageons une maison dont personne ne possède seul les clés. Le Sénégal y apportera sa langue, ses traditions, sa musique, son hospitalité et cette conviction, chère à Senghor, que l’humanité s’enrichit du donner et du recevoir. Reste à faire vivre cette ambition au-delà des discours. Il faudra veiller à ce que les filles aient toute leur place, que les jeunes en situation de handicap ne soient pas relégués aux marges, que les enfants des régions éloignées puissent eux aussi profiter de l’événement. La fierté nationale ne devrait pas être le privilège de ceux qui ont les moyens d’acheter un billet ou la possibilité de se rendre à Diamniadio. Elle grandira à mesure que chacun pourra se sentir concerné. Le 31 octobre, un président déclarera les Jeux ouverts. Mais, derrière lui, il y aura peut-être cet enfant de Ndiaganiao qui regardait Carl Lewis et Mike Powell sans savoir que cette nuit-là, quelque chose se préparait dans sa propre vie. Il y aura surtout des milliers d’autres enfants, devant les pistes et les tribunes, qui chercheront leur champion, leur discipline, leur raison d’espérer. La flamme finira par s’éteindre. C’est sa loi. La nôtre sera de ne pas laisser s’éteindre ce qu’elle aura éveillé. Car le succès véritable de Dakar 2026 ne se comptera pas seulement en médailles, en records ou en applaudissements. Il se reconnaîtra, dans dix ou vingt ans, à ces femmes et à ces hommes qui pourront dire qu’un jour, à Dakar, ils ont découvert que le monde était à leur portée. Et qu’ils avaient, eux aussi, leur place à prendre.

items.title: Maldives president, CDF Munir stress importance of strengthening defence cooperation
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu underscored the importance of strengthening bilateral defence cooperation on Wednesday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported . Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday on a three-day visit at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966. CDF Munir called on the visiting president in Islamabad, where the two leaders discussed matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment, and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation, the Radio Pakistan report said. “Both sides underscored the importance of strengthening defence cooperation, institutional linkages and professional exchanges,” it added. The CDF highlighted the “longstanding and cordial relations” between the two countries. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation and promoting peace, stability and security in the region through constructive engagement, Radio Pakistan said. It added that President Muizzu commended the professionalism of Pakistan’s armed forces and appreciated the country’s continued efforts to promote regional peace and stability. PM Shehbaz vows strengthening of bilateral relations Earlier, PM Shehbaz vowed to strengthen bilateral relations with the Maldives, as the two countries signed 20 memorandums of understanding (MoUs). Addressing a joint press stakeout following the signing of 20 wide-ranging MoUs, PM Shehbaz said, “There is no doubt that the two countries [will] keep on strengthening these relations for all time to come.” The premier extended a “very warm welcome” to the visiting dignitary and his delegation. PM Shehbaz expressed his “warmest greetings and heartfelt affection to the people of Dhivehi Raajje, the land of islands, a nation whose spirit is as vast as the ocean that surrounds it,” hailing 60 years of diplomatic ties between the two countries. The prime minister noted that he and Muizzu, in their bilateral and delegation-level talks, discussed “all important issues which have direct bearing between our two brotherly countries and of course, regional and international issues”. “I am very happy to announce that we had a wonderful session, very productive and very fruitful discussions,” he remarked. PM Shehbaz noted that the conversations encompassed “economic and trade relations, our strategic defence cooperation, our support for training of our brothers and sisters from Maldives in Pakistan in various walks of life; police, defence, education, health and many other” fields. The prime minister went on to announce that both sides had agreed to raise their bilateral trade from $13.9 million — “just a fraction of our potential” — to $200m in the next two years. Highlighting that the two South Asian countries had “very strong” relations, coupled with a “long list of mutual achievements”, PM Shehbaz said both sides noted that their ties “do not reflect the true strength of our economic cooperation”. Thanking Muizzu for his “personal support in this behalf”, the premier went on to announce that Islamabad would support Malé in promoting the plantation of 5m trees in the Maldives by providing 100,000 olive cuttings and 100,000 seeds of various plant species within a mutually decided timeframe. Referring to the MoUs signed, he affirmed that he “will be very happy to personally work with [Muizzu] to translate these written MoUs into action with prompt decision-making and speedy implementation”. The prime minister declared that Pakistan was “absolutely ready to provide technical expertise to various segments of our mutual cooperation and, above all, Pakistan is very happy to learn that Maldives is moving forward speedily to establish data centres in other places”. “This is great news, and as a matter of good luck, Pakistan has also attained a reasonable level of expertise and professional capability in this field,” he added, noting that the country had set up data centres in various locations. He offered Pakistan’s “experience and our professional capabilities in this behalf” to the Maldives. PM Shehbaz noted that a large number of Maldivian students were receiving education in Pakistani universities and colleges, particularly in the field of healthcare, and that 250 Pakistani doctors and other paramedics were serving in the Maldives. “This shall continue in future with bigger numbers so that whatever requirements you have, we as a brotherly country would be more than happy to fulfil those requirements willingly and with utmost sincerity of purpose,” the prime minister said. Speaking on international developments, PM Shehbaz commended the Maldives’ “unwavering” support for the Palestinian cause, adding that Islamabad remains fully committed to the Palestinians’ right of self-determination and the establishment of an independent state of Palestine. The premier further said he briefed Muizzu on Pakistan’s principled position on occupied Jammu and Kashmir, declaring Islamabad’s support for a peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions. “Till they have won their struggle and gotten the right of self-determination, Pakistan shall continue to support them diplomatically and, of course, support them at all international forums till they become an independent sovereign country as per UNSC resolutions, and their sacrifice will not go to waste at all,” he said. The prime minister also expressed Pakistan’s “serious concern” over India’s decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance in April 2025, pointing out that it was a violation of an international binding treaty. “Pakistan’s position is loud and clear and beyond an array of doubt; legally binding treaties must be respected and shared water resources must never be weaponised or used as an instrument of political pressure or blackmailing,” he stated. PM Shehbaz said Pakistan has made it “abundantly clear at various forums ”, including the UN General Assembly last month, that water was a “red line” for the country. “Waterflows in any canal or ocean, sea or straits, carries trade, commerce, message of prosperity and progress, and not threats, confrontations and conflicts,” he said. “Water is a lifeline for humanity […] so this should be known to all and sundry that any violation in this behalf will be regarded by Pakistan as an act of war,” the prime minister warned. Concluding his remarks, PM Shehbaz said Muizzu’s visit had given Pakistan-Maldives relations “new purpose and new momentum”. He remarked, “The same ocean that touches the shores of Karachi and Gwadar embraces the islands of the Maldives. “For centuries, its waves have carried traders, scholars and travellers between our lands. Today, they carry the renewed promise of our wonderful friendship whose finest chapters are yet to be written.” In his comments, Muizzu appreciated PM Shehbaz, the government and people of Pakistan for “their exceptional warmth and gracious hospitality”. He added that his visit coming on the 60-year mark of Pakistan-Maldives diplomatic relations made it “particularly significant”. The 60 years have been marked by warmth, friendship and shared perspectives, he said. “This visit takes place after a decade-long interval. It offers us an important opportunity not simply to celebrate the friendship of the past but to define the partnership of the future,” Muizzu said. Stressing on the close relations between the two countries, he said, “Only two such longstanding friends could have talked so widely and agreed on so much about our future together”. Muizzu said, for him, the talks represented a “clear shared ambition to move the Maldives-Pakistan partnership into a new era”. He said the discussions encompassed several sectors including trade and investment; health and education; environment, fisheries and agriculture; youth and sports; policing and defence; training and capacity-building; and tourism. The Maldivian president said he was pleased about the signing of 20 MoUs. “These memoranda will open new avenues for cooperation among multiple sectors, but agreements are meaningful only when they produce results. Our next step, of course, is to translate these understandings into tangible opportunities and meaningful benefits for the people of both nations.” Muizzu also said he endorsed the goal to take the two countries’ bilateral trade quantum from $13m to $200m in two years. “The Maldives and Pakistan are worlds of untapped potential for each other,” the Maldivian president said. He reaffirmed that the two countries would take a “firm step in the right direction”, adding that Thursday’s business forum would provide an opportunity to bring together business leaders, inventors and innovators from both countries to turn the friendship into mutually beneficial investments. He said he was encouraged by the discussions to establish direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, adding that direct flights would help support tourism as well. He further said that the two countries’ leaders saw “considerable potential in halal and Muslim-friendly tourism”. Moreover, Muizzu appreciated Pakistan’s scholarships and placements for Maldivian students, adding that the leaders would broaden the opportunities further, especially in artificial intelligence, digitisation and future technologies as well as health. “We want our next generation to be prepared for the future and be prepared to shape that future.” Muizzu stressed that climate change was “not an abstract environmental concern” for the Maldives, but “it is a direct challenge to our security, our development and our future”. He welcomed cooperation with Pakistan in areas of climate resilience, conservation, sustainable waste management and renewable energy. He thanked PM Shehbaz for his announcement of donations to help the Maldives plant 5m trees in five years. “Our nations share a commitment to advancing common interests through constructive engagements.” He said the Maldives remained committed to revitalising the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, adding that “rebuilding trust, encouraging meaningful dialogue and strengthening mutual understanding are essential to unlocking the full potential of regional cooperation”. He further expressed the Maldives’ “unequivocal and steadfast solidarity” with Palestinians and their “legitimate right to self-determination”. Muizzu also commended Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts “to promote dialogue, de-escalation, humanitarian assistance and a just and lasting peace” in the Middle East. Concluding his remarks, he said, “For 60 years, Pakistan has stood as a trusted friend of the Maldives.” The two countries have now agreed to “build a new era of partnership on the foundations of our six decades of friendship”, he said. The Maldivian president was later conferred with an honorary doctorate in politics by the International Islamic University Islamabad, with PM Shehbaz noting that the degree recognised Muizzu’s “sagacious and wise leadership and your great public service to your people in the Maldives”. 20 MoUs signed Pakistan and the Maldives signed a series of MoUs aimed at deepening bilateral relations in multiple sectors, including defence, IT, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism, among others. PM Shehbaz and Muizzu were present at the ceremony where representatives from both sides exchanged the pre-signed documents. The two countries signed an MoU on cooperation in the fields of information technology, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, digital skills, and technology and innovation. An MoU was inked to strengthen cooperation in combating illicit trafficking and abuse of narcotic drugs. The two sides also signed an MoU on social protection as well as on health cooperation and between Maldives Food and Drug Authority and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan. Both nations also signed MoUs focused on the recruitment of health professionals, strengthening defence ties and maritime security cooperation. An MoU was signed to boost agriculture cooperation, besides another one on promoting fisheries cooperation. To promote ties in technical and vocational education, an MoU on collaboration to promote technical and vocational education and training was signed, while another MoU was inked to promote educational cooperation. The representatives of Pakistan and the Maldives also exchanged MoUs on cooperation in the field of youth and sports development, air connectivity, tourism and in the field of arts, culture and heritage. The MoUs were signed between the National College of Policy and Law Enforcement of the Maldives Police Service and National Police Academy, Islamabad; Civil Service Commission of Maldives and the Federal Public Service Commission of Pakistan; and Civil Service Commission of Maldives and Civil Service Academy (CSA) of Pakistan. In order to boost commercial engagement, an MoU was signed between the Maldives State Trading Organisation (STO) and Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) for cooperation in trade of agriculture commodities, food and other products, besides signing another pact aimed at boosting cooperation in the field of environment. Prior to the MoU signing ceremony, Muizzi was welcomed at the Prime Minister House with a guard of honour. He held introductions with federal ministers while PM Shehbaz greeted the Maldivian delegation. According to a statement by PM Office (PMO), the prime minister extended a “warm welcome to the esteemed guest”, followed by a guard of honour by smartly turned-out contingents of all three armed forces. The visiting dignitary also planted a sapling at PM House, and prayers were offered for the progress and prosperity of both countries. A Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum will also be held during the visit to promote interaction between the two countries’ business communities and explore opportunities for trade and investment. President Zardari calls for stronger bilateral economic cooperation President Zardari also met his Maldivian counterpart at the President’s House in Islamabad, where he emphasised the need to translate the political goodwill between the two countries into “greater trade, investment, connectivity and people-to-people exchanges”. According to a press release by the President’s Secretariat, he also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to supporting Maldives in education, healthcare, human resource development, social protection and sustainable development. “The two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” the statement said. President Zardari reaffirmed the importance Pakistan attaches to its “longstanding fraternal relations” with the Maldives, highlighting that Muizzu’s state visit coincided with the 60-year anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries and provided “fresh momentum” to the bilateral partnership. He also recalled Pakistan’s contributions to the development of the Maldives, including the Parliament building and the School of Medicine in Malé. The press release added that both leaders expressed satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest. They recognised the disproportionate impact of climate change on vulnerable countries, particularly small island developing states and climate-vulnerable developing economies. “President Zardari expressed Pakistan’s readiness to deepen cooperation with Maldives in climate resilience, environmental protection and sustainable development, including support for President Muizzu’s Five Million Tree Initiative,” the statement said. Additionally, the leaders exchanged views on regional and international developments and underscored the importance of “dialogue, diplomacy, sovereign equality, mutual respect and peaceful resolution of disputes”, it said. They also reaffirmed their support for the rights of the Palestinian people and the establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine. According to the statement, Muizzu was accompanied by Maldivian Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam; Minister of Defence and National Service Hassan Rasheed; Minister of Homeland Security, Labour and Technology Ali Ihusaan; Minister of Economic Development, Transport and Trade Mohamed Saeed; and High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives Mohamed Thoha. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Maritime Minister Junaid Anwar, Senators Sherry Rehman and Saleem Mandviwala, former federal minister MNA Naveed Qamar, the foreign secretary, and the High Commissioner of Pakistan to the Maldives were also present, it added. The meeting was followed by a state banquet hosted by President Zardari in honour of President Muizzu and his accompanying delegation. It was attended, among others, by PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu and Commander National Strategic Command General Syed Aamer Raza. Meeting with Dar Earlier in the day, DPM Dar called on Muizzu, welcoming him and his delegation to Pakistan, the FO said on X. Dar “underscored the importance of expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment, education, climate change and tourism”, the FO said. DPM Dar also welcomed the Maldivian business delegation in the Maldives-Pakistan Business Forum and “expressed hope that B2B engagements would yield concrete trade and investment opportunities”. Muizzu, speaking to Dar, “expressed Maldives’ desire to deepen its close relations with Pakistan and explore new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation”, the FO said. Separately, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry held a meeting with Maldivian Minister for Homeland Security Ali Ihusan and exchanged views on enhancing bilateral relations and cooperation between the two countries, a statement by the interior ministry said. According to the statement, the two agreed to promote cooperation on immigration and to curb human smuggling and organised crime. It quoted Chaudhry as saying: “Pakistan values sharing experiences and security cooperation with friendly countries to promote peace and stability in the region. Pakistan wants to strengthen bilateral cooperation with the Maldives in the areas of law enforcement and internal security.” He stressed the need for cooperation between the two sides to tackle the challenges of illegal immigration and human smuggling and assured the visiting dignitary on Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s behalf of “all-possible assistance for enhancing bilateral cooperation”. Last month, the Maldives’ parliamentary speaker Abdul Raheem Abdullah met with Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir in Rawalpindi. In 2015 , former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-PM Nawaz Sharif.

items.title: Koko Fashion Show : les traditions maliennes sur le podium
items.description: © Internet Prévue ce samedi 24 octobre au Centre international de conférences de Bamako (CICB), la 6e édition de Koko Fashion Show mettra en lumière le patrimoine vestimentaire malien sous le thème « Préserver les traditions ». Défilé de mode, valorisation des savoir-faire locaux et ouverture sur la sous-région et la diaspora seront au menu de la rencontre. La mode malienne sera à l’honneur samedi 24 octobre à partir de 16 heures au Centre international de conférences de Bamako (CICB). Pour sa sixième édition, Koko Fashion Show entend faire des traditions vestimentaires un levier de promotion de l’identité culturelle et du savoir-faire des créateurs maliens. Lors d’une conférence de presse organisée mardi 20 octobre 2026, en prélude à l’événement, l’équipe de coordination a dévoilé les grandes lignes de cette édition placée sous le thème « Préserver les traditions ». Organisé par la maison de haute couture KOKO Fashion, l’événement vise à mettre en lumière la richesse culturelle du Mali à travers ses vêtements, ses tissus et ses techniques artisanales, tout en montrant leur place dans la mode contemporaine. « Nous voulons aller plus en profondeur dans les racines de notre culturalité et magnifier la tradition malienne dans toute sa splendeur », a expliqué Fatoumata Sanogo, coordinatrice générale de Koko Fashion Show. Le bogolan, le bazin et les autres tissus traditionnels occuperont une place importante dans cette édition. Au-delà de leur dimension culturelle, les organisateurs veulent rappeler leur potentiel commercial et leur capacité à conquérir de nouveaux marchés. Pour Hamadoun Bocoum, créateur de mode et promoteur de KOKO Fashion, le défilé constitue un moyen de faire connaître les créations maliennes à un public plus large, notamment à l’international. La visibilité acquise lors de ces événements peut contribuer à développer les ventes et à ouvrir des débouchés aux artisans, teinturières et créateurs. La valorisation du patrimoine passe également par sa transmission aux jeunes générations. Pour l’équipe organisatrice, connaître ses origines permet de construire son avenir sans renoncer à son identité. Les vêtements traditionnels, soulignent les responsables, peuvent aussi bien se porter au travail que lors des grandes cérémonies et des événements mondains. L’édition 2026 prévoit ainsi d’associer tradition et modernité, sans enfermer la culture malienne dans le passé. Une ouverture internationale Koko Fashion Show prévoit également un tapis rouge inspiré du Met Gala, destiné à mettre en valeur l’élégance et la créativité maliennes. Les invités sont encouragés à porter des tenues qui reflètent les traditions et les savoir-faire locaux. Le tapis rouge débutera à 16 heures, avant le lancement de la retransmission télévisée annoncé à partir de 17 h 30. Pour la première fois, l’événement sera diffusé en direct sur TM1, selon les organisateurs. Cette couverture doit permettre au public de suivre le rendez-vous au-delà de Bamako, notamment grâce aux réseaux sociaux. Plusieurs délégations étrangères sont annoncées, notamment de Guinée, de Côte d’Ivoire, de Mauritanie et du Gabon, ainsi que des participants venus des États-Unis et de France. L’équipe souhaite renforcer cette ouverture dans les prochaines années en invitant davantage de créateurs de la sous-région et de la diaspora. Les organisateurs ont également mis en avant le rôle des jeunes dans cette dynamique. Selon eux, environ 700 personnes ont participé au casting des mannequins, une démarche qui vise à offrir des opportunités au-delà des seuls professionnels du secteur. Le Roi 12 12 est le parrain de cette édition, en reconnaissance de son engagement en faveur de l’entrepreneuriat et de la jeunesse. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray defeat Lille 4-2 in Champions League thriller
items.description: Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen scored a crucial second-half goal as Galatasaray came from behind to defeat Lille 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League league phase on Wednesday. The Turkish champions recovered from a first-half deficit to secure all three points in an entertaining encounter in France, with six goals scored by both sides. Galatasaray took the lead in the second minute through Yunus Akgün, who converted a rebound from close range after Baris Yilmaz’s cross caused problems in the Lille penalty area. Lille responded five minutes later as Soriba Diaoune equalised in the seventh minute. The forward received a pass from Alexsandro, drove into the box and fired past Galatasaray goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir. The French side continued to threaten and took the lead in the 39th minute when Diaoune scored his second goal of the evening. Assisted by Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, he found space inside the penalty area before sending a first-time effort into the top-right corner. However, Galatasaray restored parity just before the break. Alexey Batrakov rose unmarked to head home Roland Sallai’s delivery in the 44th minute, ensuring both teams went into half-time level at 2-2. The visitors moved ahead again in the 52nd minute when Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer inadvertently turned the ball into his own net. Osimhen extended Galatasaray’s lead nine minutes later, finishing a swift counterattack with a first-time shot from mid-range after receiving a pass from Yilmaz. The goal made it 4-2 and gave Galatasaray a comfortable advantage as they sought to see out the contest. The Nigerian forward had earlier missed a promising opportunity in the 20th minute, while another effort was ruled out for offside in the 69th minute. However, his second-half strike proved decisive in the visitors’ victory. Lille attempted to mount a comeback, bringing on experienced striker Olivier Giroud and making further substitutions in search of goals. Galatasaray, however, remained organised defensively, with Cakir making important saves to frustrate the hosts. Despite late pressure, including a volley from Maurits Kjaergaard that narrowly missed the target, Lille could not find another goal as Galatasaray held on for a 4-2 victory. The result gave the Turkish side a significant boost in their Champions League campaign, while Osimhen’s goal underlined his importance to the team’s attacking threat. items.title: Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG
items.description: …Health minister urges Nigerians not to panic, says response coordination in place By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Federal Government has said it is collaborating with Uganda to contain the risk of an Ebola outbreak, assuring Nigerians that public health authorities are coordinating response measures. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Wednesday while fielding questions from journalists after a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. Pate was asked to react to reports that Ugandan authorities had said there was no Ebola case in their country, despite reports that a Nigerian woman had contracted the virus in Uganda. He said Nigeria was working with the East African country while taking steps to contain the reported case and prevent further transmission. “All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation of Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures to ensure that it doesn’t go into our population,” the minister said. Pate said Nigeria had competent public health institutions capable of responding to the situation, citing the country’s experience managing the 2014 Ebola outbreak. “We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions,” he said. He urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but avoid panic, advising the public to rely on information from trusted public health authorities rather than circulate unverified reports. “Nigerians should be reassured. We must be vigilant, but not panic, and people should respect public health information from trusted sources, and not spread misinformation and false rumours,” he said. The minister assured Nigerians that the government would continue to provide updates as more information became available. “We would be truthful to Nigerians with the information that we receive on a daily basis. I will be receiving a report. NCDC has an incident management system,” he added. Vanguard Newspaper The post Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CSPJ : Plus de 154.000 affaires de divorce en 2025, en hausse de 4,38 %
items.description: Le nombre d’affaires de divorce et de dissolution du mariage enregistrées par les sections de la justice de la famille au Maroc a augmenté de 4,38 % en 2025, pour atteindre 154.377 dossiers, contre 147.895 un an plus tôt. Cette progression, qui intervient après un recul en 2024, ressort du rapport annuel 2025 du Conseil supérieur du pouvoir judiciaire (CSPJ), consacré notamment à l’évolution du contentieux familial entre 2023 et 2025. Les statistiques font état de 151.168 affaires enregistrées en 2023, puis de 147.895 en 2024, avant une remontée à 154.377 en 2025. En valeur absolue, l’augmentation enregistrée entre les deux dernières années s’élève à 6.482 dossiers. La répartition des affaires met en évidence le poids prépondérant des procédures de dissolution du mariage. Sur l’ensemble des dossiers enregistrés en 2025, 112.911 concernaient des demandes de dissolution du mariage, soit 73,1 % du total, contre 41.466 affaires de divorce, représentant 26,9 %. Une activité judiciaire en progression Le nombre d’affaires jugées dans ces deux catégories a atteint 159.815 en 2025, contre 150.263 en 2024, soit 9.552 dossiers supplémentaires. Dans le même temps, le nombre d’affaires en cours s’est établi à 182.224, contre 178.290 l’année précédente. Le taux d’affaires jugées rapporté au nombre de dossiers enregistrés s’est élevé à 103,52 % en 2025, après 101,60 % en 2024 et 103,24 % en 2023. Quant à la proportion des affaires jugées parmi celles en cours, elle a atteint 87,70 %, contre 84,28 % en 2024 et 84,79 % en 2023. Le divorce par consentement mutuel largement dominant Dans le détail, les tribunaux ont enregistré 41.466 affaires de divorce en 2025, contre 40 214 en 2024 et 40.028 en 2023. Le nombre de dossiers jugés dans cette catégorie s’est établi à 42.832, contre 40.771 un an auparavant. Les affaires en cours ont, pour leur part, atteint 44.734. Le divorce par consentement mutuel domine très largement cette catégorie. Avec 40.211 affaires recensées en 2025, il représente 96,97 % de l’ensemble des dossiers de divorce. Le nombre de ces procédures s’élevait à 38.858 en 2024 et à 38.783 en 2023. Les autres formes de divorce demeurent nettement moins fréquentes. Les tribunaux ont enregistré 1.173 affaires de divorce avant la consommation du mariage en 2025, contre 1.217 en 2024. Le divorce révocable a concerné 48 affaires, tandis que le divorce par « khol « , qui implique une contrepartie financière versée par l’épouse, en a représenté 33. Une seule affaire relevait du divorce par délégation, lorsque le mari confère à son épouse le droit de mettre fin au mariage. Les procédures pour discorde concentrent 97,82 % des dissolutions Les demandes de dissolution du mariage ont, quant à elles, progressé en 2025. Les tribunaux en ont enregistré 112.911, contre 107.681 en 2024 et 111.140 en 2023. Le nombre d’affaires jugées dans cette catégorie a atteint 116.983, contre 109.492 l’année précédente, tandis que les dossiers en cours se sont élevés à 137.490. La dissolution du mariage pour discorde, dite « Chiqaq « , constitue de loin le principal motif invoqué. Avec 110.454 affaires enregistrées en 2025, elle représente 97,82 % de l’ensemble des procédures de dissolution. Cette catégorie comptait 104.898 dossiers en 2024 et 107.679 en 2023. Les autres motifs restent marginaux au regard du volume global. En 2025, les tribunaux ont recensé 1.406 affaires relevant de la catégorie générale ou non précisée, 531 demandes fondées sur l’absence du conjoint et 456 sur le préjudice. Le défaut d’entretien a donné lieu à 20 affaires, tandis que 32 dossiers concernaient un vice ou un défaut. Onze affaires étaient liées à l’abstinence conjugale et à l’abandon du foyer. Enfin, une seule procédure portait sur le manquement du mari à l’une des clauses du contrat de mariage. The post CSPJ : Plus de 154.000 affaires de divorce en 2025, en hausse de 4,38 % appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ebola: Oyo activates surveillance network in 33 LGAs
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has activated disease surveillance networks across its 33 local government areas and prepared its Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo as part of emergency measures against a possible Ebola Virus Disease outbreak. The government, however, assured residents that no confirmed case had been recorded in the state. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi, gave the assurance on Wednesday during an interview with journalists in her office, according to a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade. Ajetunmobi urged residents to remain calm but vigilant, stressing that the absence of a confirmed case should not lead to a relaxation of preventive measures. She disclosed that the Ministry of Health had begun preparations since June 2026 to strengthen the state’s readiness to respond to potential outbreaks of Ebola and other infectious diseases, including diphtheria. According to her, the government had adopted the One Health approach, which promotes collaboration across human, animal and environmental health sectors, to improve disease surveillance, preparedness and emergency response. She said the initiative involved collaboration with the Ministries of Information, Agriculture and Environment, as well as the Epidemiology Unit of the University College Hospital, Ibadan. The commissioner explained that the coordinated approach was designed to strengthen disease monitoring and response mechanisms across the state’s 33 local government areas. As part of the preparedness measures, she said disease surveillance units had been activated across the local government areas, while Information, Education and Communication materials on Ebola transmission, prevention and emergency contact channels had been distributed to health facilities. Ajetunmobi added that infection prevention and control measures had been reinforced in healthcare facilities, with health workers directed to maintain a high index of suspicion for patients presenting symptoms that could indicate Ebola infection. She emphasised that strict compliance with infection prevention protocols, including the appropriate use of personal protective equipment, was essential to protect healthcare workers and prevent possible transmission within medical facilities. The commissioner warned that Ebola symptoms could initially resemble those of malaria and might be mistaken for a less serious illness. She urged anyone experiencing sudden fever, severe headache, joint or muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, extreme tiredness, abdominal pain or unexplained bleeding to seek medical attention promptly. According to her, the incubation period for Ebola Virus Disease ranges from two to 21 days, making it important for people who develop suspicious symptoms to report to a health facility or the appropriate public health authority without delay. On the state’s capacity to manage suspected infections, Ajetunmobi said trained healthcare personnel, including laboratory teams responsible for sample collection and testing, were available to respond to potential cases. She added that the Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo had been prepared as part of the state’s emergency response arrangements. The commissioner said the ministry was also intensifying public enlightenment and risk communication to educate residents on how Ebola spreads, the precautions required to reduce infection risks and the importance of promptly reporting suspected cases. She stressed that effective prevention and containment would require sustained cooperation among government agencies, healthcare workers, the media and communities. “The Government of Oyo State is taking proactive steps to ensure that the state is adequately prepared to respond to any potential outbreak,” she said. Reiterating that no confirmed Ebola case had been recorded in Oyo, Ajetunmobi urged residents to avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary panic. She advised residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers where appropriate. Residents were also cautioned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Ebola patients, as well as materials that might have been contaminated. The commissioner further urged anyone experiencing symptoms suggestive of Ebola to contact a health facility or the relevant public health authority immediately rather than attempt to manage the symptoms without professional medical advice. Arrupe Jesuit Institute to strengthen advocacy and youth empowerment
items.description: The Arrupe Jesuit Institute (AJI) has outlined plans to expand its advocacy and youth empowerment programmes under a new strategic plan aimed at increasing its impact on Ghanaian society. The Institute’s Director, Fr Bernard Jado, SJ, and Head of Programmes, Gifty Appea, presented the priorities to the Superior General of the Society of Jesus, Fr Arturo Sosa, SJ, during his visit to the Institute in Accra on 13 October 2026. The presentation reviewed AJI’s work, traced its origins and outlined its priorities under the 2026–2029 Strategic Plan. Its advocacy programmes will focus on human rights, gender-based violence, child protection, safeguarding, refugee and migrant rights, education and environmental protection. AJI plans to advance these priorities through policy dialogues, public advocacy campaigns, institutional training and contributions to public debate. It also intends to translate research findings into policy briefs and create opportunities for engagement with policymakers. Youth empowerment, the second pillar of the plan, will cover leadership development, ethical and civic education, financial empowerment, livelihood initiatives and youth-led community projects. The Institute also plans to strengthen its alumni network to sustain engagement with young people beyond individual programmes. AJI has already undertaken environmental advocacy through its Environmental Policy Dialogues, organised in collaboration with the Catholic Youth Network for Environmental Sustainability in Africa (CYNESA-Ghana). These engagements have addressed illegal small-scale mining, ecological responsibility and the vision outlined in Pope Francis’ encyclical, Laudato Si’ . The Institute’s research has also explored migration, integral ecology and Christianity in Africa, examining structural injustices and possible responses. Through its formation programmes, AJI engages Catholic lay professionals and young people on Catholic Social Teaching, ethics and leadership. Its IYNIGO initiative supports youth empowerment, while its Faith in the Public Sphere programme provides a platform for dialogue on Christian witness, professional engagement and the common good. However, Fr Jado identified limited and unpredictable programme funding, lean staffing and gaps in organisational systems as constraints on the continuity and expansion of the Institute’s work. To address these challenges, he said AJI was seeking to diversify its funding sources beyond individual projects and strengthen staffing, governance, monitoring and evaluation, knowledge management and its digital presence. He also highlighted the importance of strategic partnerships with universities, other Jesuit institutions, dioceses, Catholic professionals, youth networks and policy actors. Fr Sosa commended the Institute’s work and encouraged its leadership to pursue financial sustainability to ensure the continuity of its programmes and the long-term fulfilment of its mission. Conceived in November 2018 as an initiative of the Society of Jesus’ North-West Africa Province, AJI was established as a platform for research, formation and social action. Named after Jesuit priest Pedro Arrupe, the Institute seeks to analyse challenges facing Ghanaian and African societies and propose solutions informed by Catholic Social Teaching.

items.title: ‘Corporate Ghana must step up’ – Bel Aqua urges business community to invest in youth mental health
items.description: Corporate Ghana is being challenged to step up investment in mental health support for young people facing depression, grief, and societal pressures, warning that many lack safe spaces to speak openly or access professional help. The call from premium bottled water brand Bel Aqua coincides with its 15th anniversary of operations in Ghana. The company’s push follows the fourth edition of its mental health initiative, which brought together students, corporate workers, and members of the public for free consultations with psychologists and psychiatrists. Speaking at the fourth edition of Bel Aqua’s mental health outreach—which provided free, confidential consultations with psychologists and psychiatrists for students, workers, and the general public—Head of Marketing Chris Addo Sarkodie urged the business community to intervene. “I think 60 per cent of the people that we’ve had today are coming from the universities. And if you listen to them sharing their testimonies and their challenges, I think as a country we need to pay attention to them,” Sarkodie said. To address the gap directly, Bel Aqua announced plans to roll out mobile mental health clinics, taking certified psychologists and psychiatrists directly into educational institutions and workplaces across the country. According to World Health Organization (WHO) estimates, roughly 13 per cent of Ghana’s population—over 4 million people—live with a mental health condition. However, due to severe infrastructure shortages and high social stigma, an estimated 98 per cent of Ghanaians requiring mental healthcare receive no formal medical treatment. Ghana currently operates with fewer than 60 practicing psychiatrists nationwide, creating a critical shortage of professional support for young people facing depression, grief, and societal pressures.

items.title: Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has said the wisdom and moral clarity of the late Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti will be greatly missed in Nigeria’s political landscape. Fasoranti, an elder statesman and leader of the Yoruba socio-political group, Afenifere, died at the age of 100. In a tribute, Tunji-Ojo said he joined the nation in mourning the late statesman with a heavy heart, describing his death as a significant loss to the country. “In him, Nigeria has lost a true leader and an enduring symbol of our democratic journey,” the minister said. He described Fasoranti’s century-long life as one anchored on selfless service, adding that his legacy stood as a testament to principled leadership. According to Tunji-Ojo, the late elder statesman was a lifelong disciple of the sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and a longstanding leader of Afenifere. He said Fasoranti remained steadfast in his advocacy for justice, true federalism and the dignity of the Yoruba people, while also upholding national unity and democratic values. The minister said the late Afenifere leader’s contributions to the political evolution of Ondo State and Nigeria would remain indelible. He recalled that Fasoranti was recently celebrated in Lagos on attaining the age of 100, describing the occasion as a rare honour that reflected the respect he commanded across generations and political divides. “Only recently, we gathered in Lagos to celebrate him as a centenarian; a rare honour that underscored the depth of respect he commanded across generations and political divides. That celebration of a life well lived now turns to solemn reflection,” he said. Tunji-Ojo extended his condolences to the Fasoranti family, the people of Ondo State, members of Afenifere and all those inspired by the late elder statesman’s life. “May the Almighty grant his soul eternal rest and comfort those he left behind. Adieu, Pa Fasoranti. Your legacy of courage, service, and integrity endures,” the minister said. The post Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Misinformation, false promises fuel irregular migration — FG
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Federal Government has identified misinformation and false promises as major drivers of irregular migration, warning that decisions based on misleading information can expose prospective migrants to serious risks and devastating consequences. The warning was contained in a speech by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), Kemi Nandap, at a Stakeholder Sensitisation and Engagement Seminar in Abuja on Wednesday. Nandap, who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said people migrated in pursuit of education, employment, safety and better opportunities, but stressed the need for accurate information to guide their decisions. “Every day people choose to migrate in pursuit of education, employment, safety, and better opportunities. While these aspirations are legitimate, decisions based on misinformation, false promises, or limited awareness of safe and lawful migration pathways can expose individuals to serious risks and devastating consequences,” she said. The seminar was themed “Bridging the Information Gap: Promoting Informed, Safe and Regular Migration.” Nandap said human trafficking, migrant smuggling, travel fraud and irregular migration underscored the risks posed by inadequate information and intelligence-sharing among operational stakeholders. “Preventing these risks requires more than border control. It begins with equipping prospective migrants with accurate, timely, and reliable information to make informed decisions and pursue safe, lawful migration pathways,” she said. The NIS chief described the service as the agency with statutory responsibility for immigration control and migration management, adding that it continued to strengthen its operational capacity through institutional reforms, modern border management technologies, intelligence gathering and improved service delivery. She cited the recent deployment of the border control and immigration management system, alongside other technology-driven platforms, as evidence of the service’s efforts to build a modern, responsive and intelligence-led immigration service. However, she acknowledged that technology alone could not address the underlying factors driving irregular migration. “Nevertheless, we recognise that even the most sophisticated border management systems cannot on their own address the underlying factors that encourage irregular migration,” she said. Nandap said the seminar was organised to develop actionable solutions to emerging challenges associated with irregular migration. She stressed that public sensitisation, community engagement and cooperation among relevant institutions must remain central to efforts to promote safe and lawful migration. “Migration sensitisation is a shared responsibility that cannot be left to the Nigeria Immigration Service alone,” she said. The comptroller-general urged government agencies, security institutions, development partners, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, educational institutions, transport operators and the media to move beyond discussions and take coordinated, practical steps to combat misinformation and raise public awareness. “Together, we must ensure that accurate migration information reaches every community, particularly those most vulnerable to exploitation and irregular migration,” she added. Also speaking, the Senior Programme Associate of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), Nnenna Onuoha, who represented the organisation’s Chief of Mission in Nigeria, Mrs Sharon Dimanche, said the partnership between the IOM and the NIS had continued to grow stronger and produce tangible results. Onuoha wished participants fruitful deliberations and actionable outcomes, expressing hope that their discussions would help make regular migration a more common and accessible option in Nigeria. The post Misinformation, false promises fuel irregular migration — FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 10 killed, 44 injured as passenger bus overturns on highway in Punjab's Rajanpur
items.description: DERA GHAZI KHAN: Ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil, Rescue 1122 said. The accident occurred in the Bangla Hidayat area at around 5:45am. The bus was reportedly speeding when it collided with the divider and toppled over. The deceased include seven men, two women and a girl, Rescue 1122 said in an incident report. Of the 44 wounded, 38 were being treated at the Rajanpur District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital, while four critically injured persons were referred to Dera Ghazi Khan and two seriously hurt to Rahim Yar Khan’s Sheikh Zayed Hospital. Rescue 1122 said it “responded promptly” upon receiving the emergency call and mobilised 10 ambulances and two rescue vehicles from Rajanpur, Jampur and Rojhan. It said 35 rescuers took part in the emergency response. Rajanpur Deputy Commissioner (DC) Imran Ranjha, the district police officer and the assistant commissioner also reached the site to oversee the situation and coordinate the response. Later, Umerkot SHO Shakeel Dreshak told Dawn that a case had been registered at his police station, in which the bus driver was also named. The first information report (FIR), seen by Dawn , was registered on the complaint of Sub-Inspector Shakeel Abbas and invoked Sections 279 (rash driving or riding on a public way), 322 (unintentional murder) and 337 (causing injury to head or face) of the Pakistan Penal Code. The FIR said the bus, which was travelling at a high speed, hit a divider on a road, turned on its side. The complainant accused the driver of negligence. DC Ranjha initially told Dawn that the bus driver had fled the scene after the incident, as well as the bus’s owner. He later told Dawn that the driver had been taken into police custody and was being treated at a hospital. On Monday, a road accident on Multan’s Bosan Road claimed the lives of five men in their 20s early after their speeding Toyota Corolla hit a road divider before crashing into the wall of a nearby plot and catching fire. According to Rescue 1122 , around 1,352 road traffic incidents, resulting in an average of 14 deaths, are reported per day across Punjab.

items.title: Bel-Aqua’s Healing Together Vigil draws over a thousand for an evening of music and mental health dialogue
items.description: Over a thousand people gathered at Alliance Française in Accra on Friday, 16 October 2026, for Bel-Aqua’s Healing Together Vigil 4.0, an evening combining mental health conversations with live music, comedy and community connection. Held under the theme “Every Mind Has a Story… Respond with Hope”, the fourth edition formed part of Bel-Aqua’s Take a Break initiative. It followed the Healing Together Walk on 3 October, extending the campaign’s call for people to make time for their mental well-being and support those around them. At the heart of the vigil was a message that went beyond encouraging people to speak about their struggles: the response they receive matters just as much. The campaign called for listening without judgment and approaching difficult conversations with empathy, care and hope. Guests were welcomed into an experience zone featuring a Story Wall, hydration and red-carpet interviews before Kwan Pa opened the stage programme with a musical performance. A mental health conversation moderated by Yaa Bitha brought together Fafa Gozo, founder of the Dzidula Pink Foundation; Dr. Seth Mawusi-Asafo, clinical psychologist and lecturer; Dr. Masha Bashiru, senior clinical and health psychologist; and Jahara Osman, founder of Mental Health Forum. The session brought professional and advocacy perspectives into the evening’s programme, placing mental health dialogue alongside entertainment. Host Lekzy DeComic guided proceedings with comedy interludes, while performances by Mr. Drew, Kojo Blak and Efya added to the evening’s entertainment. The evening also featured addresses by Christopher Addo-Sarkodie, Head of Marketing, and Oscar Adaadaare, Regional Sales Manager, both of Bel Aqua, as well as Dr. Vivian Aba Dadzie, Deputy CEO of the Ghana Mental Health Authority. DJ Sleek led the after-party, giving guests an opportunity to unwind and connect. The vigil complemented the campaign’s earlier walk from Ayi Mensah to Peduase, where activities included health screening and access to psychologists and psychiatrists. Together, the two events placed mental well-being within community life, combining opportunities for connection with conversations about support. Through its Take a Break initiative, Bel-Aqua continues to encourage people to make room for their mental well-being. This year’s vigil reinforced the campaign’s central appeal: beyond asking someone to share their story, be prepared to listen and respond with hope.

items.title: Ebola: Edo urges calm, compliance with safety guidelines
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Edo State Government has urged residents to remain calm and comply with public health guidelines following reports of a confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Cyril Oshiomhole, made the call on Wednesday during a press briefing on the reported case. Represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health, Dr Eighemherio Ikhumosa, Oshiomhole said the state government was monitoring developments in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). He described the development as a serious public health concern, adding that the ministry was engaging relevant health agencies and partners to strengthen preparedness and response measures. The commissioner advised residents to avoid contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons, wash their hands regularly with soap and water, and use appropriate alcohol-based hand sanitisers. He also warned against handling the personal belongings of confirmed cases without proper protective measures. Oshiomhole urged anyone who developed symptoms such as fever, weakness, headache or muscle pain, particularly after possible exposure to the virus, to seek immediate medical attention and follow the guidance of health professionals. He further cautioned residents against spreading unverified information that could cause unnecessary panic or undermine public health efforts. The commissioner urged the public to remain vigilant, stay calm and adhere to preventive measures as health authorities monitor the situation. items.title: Ebola Scare: NEMA DG urges calm, warns against contact with suspected cases
items.description: …Says confirmed FCT patient isolated as authorities intensify contact tracing By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Director-General of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Mrs Zubaida Umar, has urged Nigerians to remain calm and observe preventive measures following the reported confirmation of an Ebola Virus Disease case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Umar warned against panic, misinformation and stigmatisation, saying the patient had been isolated and was receiving medical care, while contact tracing and surveillance continued. In a public advisory, the NEMA chief called for increased public awareness and cooperation with health officials, stressing that early detection and responsible behaviour were critical to preventing further transmission. She said the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), in collaboration with the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant agencies, were leading the response. According to her, NEMA remained prepared to provide coordination and emergency support within the country’s emergency management framework as required. “Our most important message to Nigerians is: remain calm, remain vigilant and follow official health advice. There is no need for panic,” she said. How Nigerians can avoid infection Umar said Ebola could spread through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who was ill, as well as through contaminated materials. She urged Nigerians to observe personal hygiene and take precautions against possible exposure. She advised citizens to wash their hands frequently with soap and running water or use alcohol-based hand sanitisers, while avoiding direct contact with the bodily fluids of anyone suspected of having the disease. The NEMA director-general also cautioned against unsafe contact with wild animals, including handling dead animals. She warned against touching or preparing the bodies of people suspected of dying from Ebola, saying such bodies should be handled by trained health authorities to minimise the risk of transmission. Umar further advised anyone who developed symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting or diarrhoea after possible exposure to seek medical guidance immediately. Contact tracing, public cooperation critical The NEMA chief identified public cooperation as essential to containing the disease, urging anyone approached by contact-tracing teams to provide accurate information and comply with instructions from public health officials. She also warned against spreading unverified reports, noting that rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation could undermine efforts to contain the outbreak. “For official advice or to report a suspected case, the NCDC toll-free number is 6232,” she said. Nigeria’s 2014 experience offers hope Umar recalled Nigeria’s successful containment of Ebola in 2014, saying the experience demonstrated the importance of early detection, effective contact tracing, responsible public behaviour and coordinated action among relevant institutions. She assured Nigerians that NEMA would continue to support the national response as required while strengthening public awareness and emergency preparedness. The advisory comes amid concern over the reported Ebola case in the FCT, with vigilance, timely reporting of suspected infections and adherence to official health guidance expected to remain central to efforts to prevent further spread. Umar urged Nigerians to stay informed through credible official channels, protect themselves and cooperate with authorities to safeguard public health. The post Ebola Scare: NEMA DG urges calm, warns against contact with suspected cases appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SENHABITAT 2026 : Dakar accueille le Salon international de l’habitat du 22 au 24 octobre
items.description: Le Salon international de l’habitat du Sénégal (SENHABITAT 2026) se tiendra du 22 au 24 octobre au King Fahd Palace, à Dakar. Placée sous le thème « L’habitat souverain : Sunu dekkuwaay », cette édition entend réunir les acteurs publics et privés autour des enjeux du logement, de l’immobilier et du développement urbain durable. Durant trois jours, le SENHABITAT 2026 offrira un cadre d’échanges et de rencontres professionnelles aux acteurs des secteurs de l’habitat, de la construction, de l’urbanisme et de l’aménagement du territoire. L’objectif est de promouvoir des solutions durables et innovantes, adaptées aux besoins des populations sénégalaises. Les discussions porteront notamment sur les défis liés au logement, à l’accès à la propriété et à la souveraineté dans le domaine de l’habitat. Le salon ambitionne également de favoriser la réflexion sur les perspectives d’un développement urbain durable au Sénégal. À travers cette rencontre, les organisateurs souhaitent mobiliser les différentes parties prenantes autour des réponses à apporter aux besoins en logement et aux enjeux de transformation des villes. La cérémonie et les activités du salon sont prévues au King Fahd Palace. L’accueil des équipes de presse est fixé à 9 h 30. C.G.D

items.title: NACOC takes drug education campaign to Diabene SHS
items.description: The Western Regional Command of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has launched a drug education and sensitisation campaign targeting newly admitted Senior High School (SHS) students to raise awareness of the dangers of drug use. The initiative seeks to equip students with accurate information to help them make responsible decisions as they adjust to the academic and social demands of senior high school. As part of the campaign, the Commission engaged students of Diabene Senior High School, educating them on the risks associated with drug use, the influence of peer pressure, and the importance of safeguarding their health, education, and future aspirations. The Commission is focusing on students at the early stages of their SHS education, recognising that the period presents an opportunity to build resilience against negative influences and encourage healthy lifestyles. The campaign forms part of NACOC’s preventive approach to tackling substance abuse, with emphasis on educating young people before they are exposed to its potential consequences. The Western Regional Command says the sensitisation exercise will be extended to other educational institutions across the region, with school authorities and relevant stakeholders expected to play a role in promoting a safer and healthier learning environment.

items.title: Ghana, UK make progress in talks to secure IELTS exemption for students, professionals – Ablakwa
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says Ghana has made significant progress in negotiations with the United Kingdom to exempt Ghanaian students and professionals from the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) examinations. In a post on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, Mr Ablakwa said discussions with the UK Foreign Secretary, Edward Miliband, had established that Ghana meets the minimum statistical threshold for English proficiency required for favourable consideration. “Thus far, we have demonstrated that Ghana meets the minimum statistical threshold in English proficiency for favourable consideration by our UK friends. Both sides remain highly optimistic,” he stated. Mr Ablakwa disclosed this after a meeting with Mr Miliband, during which the two officials reviewed bilateral relations and explored opportunities to deepen cooperation between Ghana and the UK. He said the meeting also highlighted the positive trajectory of trade and investment between the two countries. “We welcomed the impressive upward trajectory in Ghana-UK trade and investments,” he said. The discussions also covered President John Dramani Mahama’s vision for reparatory justice and prospects for broader dialogue following a United Nations resolution led by Ghana declaring the transatlantic enslavement of Africans the gravest crime against humanity. On multilateral cooperation, the two officials discussed shared priorities ahead of 2027, when Ghana is expected to chair the African Union while the UK assumes the G20 presidency. They also assessed preparations and areas of common interest ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting scheduled for next month in Antigua and Barbuda. Mr Ablakwa expressed appreciation to the UK Foreign Secretary for hosting him, reaffirming Ghana’s commitment to strengthening relations between the two countries. “I thank the outstanding Foreign Secretary for his warm hospitality. We deeply cherish our longstanding Ghana-UK relations,” he added. If secured, the proposed IELTS exemption could ease an important requirement for Ghanaian students and professionals seeking opportunities in the UK. However, Mr Ablakwa did not provide a timeline for concluding the negotiations or implementing the proposed exemption.

items.title: KNUST Engineering College launches 75th anniversary, eyes Gh¢40m innovation building
items.description: The College of Engineering at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is seeking to deepen collaboration with industry and transform academic research into practical solutions, hinting at the construction of a GH¢40 million Technology and Innovation Building. The project is in celebration of the College’s 75 years of engineering education and producing prominent and active engineering professionals for nation-building. The proposed four-to-five-storey Technology and Innovation Building would provide space for students to develop and test their ideas, while enabling companies to collaborate directly with university researchers on new technologies and products. Provost of the College, Professor Kwabena Biritwum Nyarko, says the institution’s next phase of development would depend on stronger partnerships between researchers, students and industry to develop technologies, products and services that address real-world challenges. “We are therefore not simply inviting industry to support the College. We are inviting industry to innovate with us,” he said. The launching ceremony was held under the theme “Excellence to Eminence: 75 Years of Engineering Education at KNUST”. The event brought together university authorities, industry representatives, alumni and traditional leaders, with speakers emphasising the need for engineering education to deliver greater impact beyond the classroom. The anniversary comes at a time when the College is seeking to build on its history by strengthening the connection between education, research and industry. KNUST Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, called for closer links between academic research and industry, arguing that universities must ensure their work produces tangible benefits for society. “Universities have a responsibility to generate knowledge. But they must ensure that such knowledge is translated into solutions that respond to real social needs,” he said. Professor Agyare urged industry partners to support research, provide equipment and practical training opportunities, and collaborate with the College on projects that would strengthen graduates’ employability and Ghana’s technological capacity. “For industry, the challenge is not simply to employ graduates but to help prepare them for the practical demands of the profession,” he noted. Chief Executive Officer of Associated Consultants Ltd, Ing. Kwabena Bempong, who is an alumnus of the College, said discipline and service were essential to moving from excellence to eminence. “The bridge, for me, is discipline and service, urging students to take industrial attachments seriously, learn from real projects and maintain professional integrity,” he said. He also pointed to emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, renewable energy and digital construction as areas requiring engineers who can adapt to technological change without losing sight of fundamental engineering principles. Daasebre Osei Bonsu, Paramount Chief of Asante Mampong and an alumnus of the College, called for sustained investment in research facilities, stronger international partnerships and opportunities for students to turn their ideas into viable businesses. Reflecting on his training in geomatics engineering, he highlighted the contribution of engineering knowledge to land management, infrastructure planning and national development. “The College should make its anniversary a commitment to future progress rather than simply a celebration of past achievements,” he said.
